jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.desc:
Now is an amazing time to join Nozomi Networks as we build the future of OT and IoT cybersecurity.

We defend some of the world's largest organizations and critical infrastructure in more than 68 countries and we're just getting started. Our AI-powered cybersecurity platform secures operational technology (OT) and Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructures for enterprises and government entities across energy, manufacturing, transportation, resources, and critical infrastructure.

As we expand our product portfolio, our Product Management team is hiring a Senior / Staff Product Manager to help build a new platform that will become the system of record for industrial operations: every asset, every change, every approval, and its full history, in one OT-native CMDB and service management platform.

Customers asked for this. Plant teams are tired of forcing industrial environments into IT ticketing and CMDB tools that were never built for them. Nozomi Networks already sees what is on the plant floor in real time; now we are building the platform that keeps the record and governs every change. The platform is in its design and early-access phase, shaped with enterprise and mid-market customers, and the data model is still open. You will own the problem and design the solution together with engineering.

This role starts with an advantage. CMDBs live or die on data quality, and this one sits on live, first-party asset data from Nozomi Networks sensors, so the platform can verify that what the record says matches what is actually on the network. AI is part of the core, not bolted on: agents that watch for changes, open the work, and answer questions about an asset's history.

We have deep OT expertise across the company. What this team needs now is someone who has built a CMDB before.

You could be the next "Nozomier"! If this sounds like you, read on.

**In this role, you will:**
---------------------------

Own the OT-Native Data Model

* Lead the data model for an OT-native CMDB, designed with engineering: assets, installed positions, locations and ISA-95 hierarchies (site, area, line, cell), relationships, and the full change history of every asset from installation to retirement.

* Define how the recorded state of each asset relates to what live network data shows, and what happens when they differ.

* Decide how assets the network never sees (offline equipment, spreadsheet imports) live alongside observed ones, keeping it clear which values were observed and which were only declared.

Define Identity and Reconciliation

* Partner with engineering on identity and reconciliation rules: when records from sensors, integrations, and spreadsheets describe the same physical asset, which source wins for each field, and how every value stays traceable.

* Engineering builds the matching; you define what it must get right.

Shape Workflows, Integrations, and AI

* Shape the default workflows customers start from (planned and unplanned change, vulnerability remediation, asset changes, safety approvals) on a configurable workflow engine, including what proves a change was actually done.

* Define how the platform works alongside systems customers already run, such as an existing CMDB or ITSM tool: which system owns which record, and how work flows between them.

* Help decide where an AI agent acts and where a person must approve.

Drive Decisions and Delivery

* Make the calls: own the problem, negotiate the solution with engineering, hold the line on what a release must include, and turn weeks of debate into days of decisions.

* Work directly with early-access customers to validate, learn fast, and ship.

* Collaborate daily with an engineering team based in Europe and a cross-functional product team, reporting directly to the VP of Product.

* Embody Nozomi Networks' cultural pillars, promoting transparency, trust, and accountability.

jobs.desc:
**ABOUT PEARLY**

Pearly is a high-growth B2B SaaS and payments company at a critical inflection point. With deep product-market fit and over 3,000 dental offices across DSOs, groups, and private practices on the platform, we're now looking for builders to help shepherd the next stage of growth.

Because we're lean, you won't be inheriting legacy process or systems debt. You'll be building from a clean slate: leveraging process, technology, and AI in smart, creative ways to accelerate growth and productivity across dental billing, payments, and engagement.

We are a team of high-talent, high-integrity people who genuinely enjoy the art of building and competing; honing our craft and getting better each day, both as individuals and as a team. We care deeply about good outcomes, but just as much about how we get there with smart, passionate people who hold each other to a high standard, move fast, and take pride in the work.

That's what makes Pearly feel different. The caliber of the people and the intentionality behind how we operate.

**THE ROLE**

You'll own Practice Experience: the app the practice team works in every day, the workflows inside it, and the experience around it from onboarding to daily use. Your users are the people responsible for a practice's financial performance, some living in Pearly for hours a day working a queue of accounts, others, like an owner or a CFO, checking in weekly and needing to know where things stand without digging. And it isn't one customer. It's the single-location office running its own billing, the group or DSO standardizing across dozens of locations, and the outsourced billing company working on behalf of hundreds. You own that arc for all of them without building three versions of the product.

The problems are concrete. A new customer should get live and start collecting in days, not weeks. An RCM manager should be able to set up a payment plan in under a minute without calling support. A balance sitting 60 days past due shouldn't wait for a person to decide to chase it. And a DSO rolling out location 41 shouldn't need the hand-holding location 1 did. Some of those are workflow problems, some are product we haven't built, and some are automation that should have replaced the work entirely. All of them compound directly into collections.

Part of your roadmap exists to win customers and part exists to keep them, and you should know which is which. The metrics you'll answer for are listed below. Senior here means you own it end to end, from discovery through release, without day-to-day direction. The lines around your area are thin on purpose. With a lean product bench, breadth matters, and you'll own features that reach into Payments, Onboarding, and Integrations.

**WHAT YOU'LL OWN**

Getting Live and Getting Unstuck. Onboarding and support are product surfaces, not someone else's problem. Own what gets configured versus defaulted, how fast a new customer connects their PMS and reaches value, and the in-product guidance that replaces a training call.

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. AI is moving off the screen and into physical operations and Samsara is building it. If you want to be a product manager enabling the transformation behind how the real world works, join us.

We connect the vehicles, equipment, sites, and people behind the physical operations that power our economy. Our platform collects more than 30 trillion data points a year from vehicles that travel 99.9% of U.S. roads, and we design our own hardware to capture it. We hire product managers into Samsara first and match you with the team and problem where you'll have the most impact. Problem spaces evolve consistently here and what's most important is your excitement about what and how Samsara is building.

Accumulus Technologies helps life sciences companies reduce regulatory friction, shorten timelines, and lower execution risk across product development and lifecycle management—delivering measurable and transformational ROI. jobs.desc:
Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry's digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity.

We are hiring a Staff Product Manager to own that experience end to end. You sit between Sales and the quoting teams and you serve the customers who matter most to Xometry. Your job is to rethink how a request becomes a priced quote: every channel it can arrive through, every hand-off between a person and a system, and every step that does not need a human at all. You will design the agents that read the request, build the quote, and propose the price, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations that let those agents work across our quoting systems and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) platform, and the staff tools where people review what the agents did and decide what they should not. The measure is simple: how fast, how accurately, and with how little effort our best customers get a quote they can act on.

This role sits in the Pricing and Manufacturability (P&M) group alongside the product managers for cost prediction, pricing, and Design for Manufacturability (DFM), and reports to the head of P&M product.

You will be given a metric and a problem space, not a fully scoped backlog. Comfort defining your own roadmap from ambiguous signals is a requirement, not a bonus.

This role requires a hybrid schedule (3 days a week) at our Waltham, MA or North Bethesda, MD office location.

**How You'll Contribute**

* **Own the request-to-quote experience for our most important customers.** Map every path a quote request takes today, from the moment a customer emails, texts, uploads, or sends an agent, through Sales, quoting, pricing review, and back to the customer. Know the behind-the-scenes steps better than anyone outside the teams that run them. Remove the steps that do not need to exist. Your scorecard: quote turnaround time, cost per quote, quote accuracy, and quote-to-order conversion on the human-assisted path.
* **Redesign the funnel, not just the tools.** Treat each intake channel as a pathway with its own drop-offs and its own fix. Decide where a request should be read by an agent, where it should be routed to a person, and where the customer should be able to self-serve without either. Build the pathways so a request arrives structured, complete, and already half-priced by the time a human sees it.
* **Make agents do the work people should not have to.** Own the roadmap for agentic quoting: agents that read a request and its files and build the quote, assistants that propose margin and lead time, and automation that promotes human-priced parts into the instant-pricing engine over time. Decide what the agent does, what the human confirms, and what stays human. Define "good" and "failure" for every AI feature before engineering starts, and hold that bar through launch and after.
* **Connect the agents to the business through MCP and the ERP.** Own the integration layer that lets agents and people exchange work across Salesforce, our quoting systems, file storage, and the ERP: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, tool definitions, permissions, and the audit trail that shows who (or what) changed a quote and why. The exchange between humans and agents is a product surface; design it like one.
* **Build the staff tools the quoting and sales teams actually use.** Own the internal quote review, pricing, and quote summary tools. Treat adoption as the product metric: a tool the team routes around has failed, regardless of what shipped.
* **Instrument everything.** Every human pricing decision (override, margin change, lead-time adjustment) becomes structured data that improves the next prediction and the next agent run. Write your own queries, build your own dashb

jobs.title: Senior Technical Product Manager, Internal Software
jobs.desc:
**About Fervo Energy**
----------------------

Fervo Energy (NASDAQ: FRVO) is a modern power company developing next-generation geothermal resources to meet the growing demand for affordable, reliable, 24/7 carbon-free energy. Our mission is to transform geothermal into America's most dependable and affordable source of clean, around-the-clock power. By combining innovations in horizontal drilling, fiber-optic sensing, and advanced reservoir engineering, Fervo has developed a repeatable approach to building utility-scale enhanced geothermal systems. Our flagship Cape Station development in Utah is planned to deliver 500 MW of firm, carbon-free power, and we are advancing a development pipeline of more than 50 GW. Join us and work alongside world-class engineers, geoscientists, operators, project builders, and business leaders working to make geothermal a cornerstone of a more reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy future.

**Position Description**
------------------------

The Senior Technical Product Manager, Internal Software will lead the development of internal software tools across Fervo. This role is the connective tissue between our internal users and the engineers building the tools they need, turning ambiguous internal needs into clear, actionable product requirements. Unlike a traditional product role focused on external customers, you will work across engineering, construction, drilling, completions, supply chain, finance, and operations to understand how work gets done and to identify the workflows that slow execution.

The ideal candidate is a deeply technical product manager, or a former software engineer who can code, partner credibly with engineers, and move comfortably between product strategy and software execution. Experience in geothermal, energy, drilling, or construction is not required. In the near term, this role will own product direction, technical scoping, delivery, adoption, and build-vs-buy decisions, and over time has the potential to evolve into leadership of Fervo's internal software development team as the function scales. Beyond strong software judgment and product instincts, the ideal candidate brings comfort with ambiguity and the ability to build useful tools quickly in a fast-moving environment.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* **Product Ownership:** Own internal software product development from idea to adoption. Work closely with teams across Fervo to understand their workflows, pain points, operating rhythms, and decision-making needs, and translate ambiguous business problems into clear product requirements, technical specs, user stories, and success criteria. Design for a connected software ecosystem rather than one-off applications, ensuring tools integrate with existing systems, data sources, and future internal platforms. Measure success through adoption, workflow improvement, and business impact, not just shipped features.
* **Engineering Partnership:** Partner closely with software engineers, contractors, and technical partners to scope, sequence, and deliver internal tools. Bring enough software fluency to evaluate technical tradeoffs, ask tough questions, and make pragmatic implementation decisions. Write clear technical product requirements, and own delivery cadence, backlog management, sprint planning, stakeholder updates, and risk escalation. Contribute technically when helpful, especially in early prototyping, agentic coding workflows, technical review, or lightweight implementation support.
* **Tools for Fast-Moving Teams:** Develop software that improves how Fervo manages complex work across engineering, construction, project execution, documentation, scheduling, modeling, procurement, and operations. Identify where teams rely on manual processes, disconnected data, or inefficient tools, and build products that are simple, usable, and practical. Sit with users before and after launch, and create feedback loops that drive continuous product improvement.

You've worked shoulder to shoulder with the ads and monetization side, built genuine empathy for why the business needs to extract value from search, and you know firsthand how sponsored content, ad load, and paid-organic blending actually behave. You know that great search monetization makes results better, not worse, and you've seen engagement and revenue grow together when both sides pull in the same direction. This is a multi-year rebuild rather than a tuning exercise, and you won't do it alone: dedicated data science partners, ML engineers with search backgrounds, and design coverage are committed to the team. Ideally, you've also built beyond search and bring the range of a generalist athlete who can flex across consumer, marketplace, and business-facing problems. You'll partner closely with engineering, data science, research, design, and PMM to turn that thinking into shipped experiments with real, measurable impact.

At Nextdoor, we operate in an AI-first environment and expect every team member to actively use AI tools as part of their workflow. We aren't looking for prompt engineers; we’re looking for people who use tools like Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Glean to challenge their own thinking and take full ownership of AI-assisted outputs.

TheImpact You’ll Make

  • Build the missing foundation first: define the metric that tells us whether a neighbor found what they came for, and make it the measure every experiment and ship call answers to. It does not exist today, and it's the most important thing you'll deliver in your first six months
  • Own the Search rebuild end to end, organic and monetized together, from query understanding and retrieval to ranking, result quality, and how the page comes together
  • Make the majority of searches work: most queries are a neighbor looking for a post, a person, a place, or an answer, with no commercial intent, and today we fail them too often
  • Partner with dedicated data science and ML engineering on query understanding, retrieval, and ranking, going deep on the mechanics when the details matter
  • Design how organic and sponsored content blend

We're energized by new challenges and new possibilities-and we're just getting started!

We have an opening for a Principal Platform Product Manager to lead the definition of Constant Contact's core services, with particular focus on authentication and billing. These are the services every product we ship is built on: how a customer signs in, what their plan lets them do, and how what they use turns into revenue. The first job is billing. We are moving from an in-house billing system to Stripe Billing, and hundreds of thousands of small businesses count on us getting it right. Alongside it, we are modernizing identity: sign-in, single sign-on, and the account and access model behind them. As those stabilize, the scope of this role grows with the business. Entitlements, account structure, partner and reseller models, and whatever core service we need next are all fair game for someone who has earned the trust to take them on.

You will partner with our Billing Infrastructure and Growth & Enablement engineering teams and with Security, and work closely with Finance, FP&A, RevOps, Support, Sales and our Growth PMs.

Success in this role looks like a clean move to Stripe, an identity platform that is simple for customers and safe for the business, and core services the rest of the company can build on without waiting on you.

* **Own Billing & Payments Strategy:** Set direction for subscriptions, plans and pricing, invoicing, payment methods, payment recovery, refunds and account changes. Decide the sequence and make the trade-offs explicit.

* **Make Billing Data Trustworthy:** Define the billing data model and the source of truth across our systems so Finance's reporting, revenue recognition and audits reconcile without manual work. You define how the data should look; Finance and our data team own the reporting built on it.

Our BHAG: 1+ job per household, every year. Getting there means winning on four fronts at once: more customers, more Pros, excellent service for both sides, and an AI-run company that moves faster than its size should allow.

**About the First Service Experience at LawnStarter**

Every new customer meets us the same way. They land on our home page or marketing site, then move through a signup and booking flow where they get a quote, pick a service and a schedule, and pay. That flow runs across all three brands and brings in most of the company's new customers.

We built it many years ago. It's too long, and we lose customers at too many steps. So the real question isn't how to remove a step. It's whether the experience designed still makes sense at all, or whether it should be rethought entirely as an AI-native, agentic experience.

**The Role**

You'll own the consumer's first service experience: everything from the moment someone first encounters LawnStarter through signing up and booking their first service. You'll decide what that experience should become, then build it with engineering, design, operations, marketing, and data.

This is not a funnel-optimization job. We want someone who looks at a five-year-old flow, asks what a homeowner would want if we started from nothing today, and then ships the answer.

As Lead PM, you're an individual contributor with Lead-level scope and no direct reports. You'll work closely with the Consumer Experience lead, the Pro Experience PM, the Pricing PM, and the Conversational AI & Agents lead. You'll report to the Sr. Director of Product.

**What makes this role different:**

* **A rebuild, not a tune-up.** You're rethinking the experience from first principles, not polishing the one we have.
* **AI-native from the first screen.** You'll decide whether a form is even the right way to sign up anymore.
* **Every new customer passes through your work.** Across three brands, this is how people meet LawnStarter.

**What You'll Own**

* **The vision:** What the first service experience should become, and the plan to get there.
* **The home page and marketing site:** The first impression, and the first decision a customer makes about us.
* **Signup and booking for all three brands:** LawnStarter, Lawn Love, and Home Gnome.
* **Funnel data:** The numbers that show where customers move forward and where they leave.
* **Quotes, services, and scheduling:** How a customer gets a price, picks a service, and chooses when it happens.
* **Payment:** Checkout, including Apple Pay and Google Pay.

**Problems to Solve**

**Deciding whether today's experience should exist at all.**  
You'll start from what a homeowner needs to book their first service and work backward. Every step we have today has to earn its place again, and you'll defend each call with evidence.

**Designing an AI-native, agentic way to sign up.**  
Someone who wants their lawn mowed shouldn't have to learn our product to book it. What can an agent handle for them, and where does a person still want control? You'll answer with prototypes in front of real customers, not opinions in a meeting.

**Rebuilding without breaking what works.**  
This flow brings in most of our new customers. You'll need a path that proves the new experience works with real customers before it replaces the old one. Bold and careful at once: that's the job.

**Moving levers you don't own.**  
Signup touches pricing, Pro supply, and operations. Change how customers book and you change what Pros see and how jobs get priced. You'll work through the people who own those levers and bring them along on a vision that changes their world too.

Description:

**Balanced Body** is an energetic, environmentally sensitive company that is growing! Balanced Body leads the world in providing Pilates equipment and education.

**This role requires hands-on experience with discrete, manufactured products — not software, SaaS, apps, or other digital products. Candidates whose product background is entirely digital will not have the manufacturing exposure this role requires.**

**What is the role**

We are looking for a Product Lead to own product strategy across Balanced Body's product lines. You will set the product roadmap, decide what stays in the line and what gets cut, and define positioning, pricing, and features for new and existing products. This is a strategic ownership role — you decide what gets built and why.

You will work closely with our Program Manager (Manufacturing), who owns execution once product direction is set. The two roles operate as peers: you are not their manager, and they independently own how initiatives get delivered once you've defined what they are and why they matter.

In addition to ongoing roadmap and portfolio management, you'll lead several new product initiatives currently in development, spanning both hard goods and soft goods categories. You will also build Balanced Body's formal innovation cycle — a repeatable process the company will use going forward to source, evaluate, and prioritize new product ideas.

This is a product strategy role, but it is grounded in hands-on manufacturing experience. You should have worked directly on discrete physical products — materials, bills of materials, tooling, supplier and factory relationships, production feasibility, cost, and lead times — so that your roadmap and pricing decisions reflect how things are actually made.

**What you'll do**

* Own and maintain the product roadmap across Balanced Body's product lines.

* Lead new product initiatives from concept through definition, including several projects currently in development across hard goods and soft goods categories.
* Partner with the Program Manager (Manufacturing) as a peer: you define product direction and requirements; they own execution, scheduling, and cross-functional delivery. This role does not direct the Program Manager's day-to-day work.
* Design and implement a formal, repeatable innovation cycle for Balanced Body — a standard process for sourcing, evaluating, and prioritizing new product concepts across the organization.
* Use customer feedback, market research, and competitive analysis to inform roadmap, pricing, and positioning decisions.
* Partner with engineering, suppliers, and manufacturing early in concept development to validate feasibility, materials, tooling, cost, and production constraints before committing a product to the roadmap.
* Partner with marketing and sales to align product positioning and pricing with go-to-market strategy.
* Present roadmap, portfolio, and pricing recommendations to leadership for approval.
* Serve as the internal subject matter expert on product strategy and the reasoning behind product decisions.

jobs.desc:
**Join us on the Product Management team as a Senior Product Manager – LPG and Fuels & Lubricants.** In this role, you will own the Anova Unify product direction for the LPG and Fuels & Lubricants (F&L) markets, translating a deep understanding of how propane, fuel, and lubricant distributors run their operations into software that helps them serve their customers more efficiently and grow. You’ll set the vertical strategy, lead customer discovery, and own the go-to-market for your markets, partnering closely with the platform Product Management team, Hardware Product Management, and Engineering. **Start your journey with Anova today!**

  

**Outcomes you’ll own:**

  

* **Anova leads customer insight amongst the IoT market.** Your passion for understanding LPG and F&L distributors, their delivery and supply operations, and how IoT transforms their business will keep Anova the company that best understands how IoT creates value for our customers as they serve their own.
* **Greater than 90% customer device productivity.** Keep customers’ device portfolios live, healthy, and reporting by solving real, value-adding problems and delivering best-in-class reliability, so customers see clear reason to keep every device active.
* **Net Revenue Retention and customer value.** Customers in your markets renew, expand, and advocate. You own the product-side inputs to NRR (adoption, engagement, and satisfaction), track measurable customer outcomes such as reduced operating costs and faster time-to-value, and make disciplined trade-offs to protect gross margin.
* **Set domain strategy.** Define the multi-year product vision for the LPG and F&L markets, grounded in customer insight, competitive dynamics, industry trends, and Anova’s strategic priorities. Build an evidence-backed roadmap the organization trusts, defining the metric before you ship the feature. Partner with platform Product Management to shape shared capabilities around your markets’ needs, and keep Engineering, Customer Success, Sales, and Marketing aligned on what’s being built and why so ambiguity is resolved upstream, not during delivery.
* **Lead deep customer discovery.** Design and run ongoing discovery programs with LPG and F&L customers, including interviews, site visits, usage analysis, and win/loss reviews, and stay engaged with the industry through trade associations and events. Develop a differentiated point of view on what these customers need, what they’ll pay for, and what will create durable competitive advantage in your markets.
* **Drive AI-first product thinking.** Identify where ML and AI (forecasting, anomaly detection, decision support, workflow automation) create meaningful customer value in your markets. Decide what to build, buy, or partner for, and move it from idea to shipped capability, while using AI as leverage in your own research, synthesis, drafting, and analysis.
* **Partner with engineering on architecture and trade-offs.** Engage credibly on system design, API contracts, data models, and integration architecture. Make principled trade-offs between scope, speed, and technical quality, and document your reasoning.

Your products will be delivered as part of a larger integrated solution, so you’ll own how they connect to upstream source products, the shared data platform, and the client and internal experiences that use them.

* Define a 1-3 year vision and an outcomes-focused roadmap for client and program analytics. Base it on client needs, program priorities, and market trends, and communicate tradeoffs to leadership, clients, and partners.

* Partner with data engineering and platform teams on how data is ingested, modeled, governed, and served on Databricks, turning business needs into clear data product requirements.
* Work directly with clients, program managers, and client success teams to understand reporting needs, validate solutions, and run roadmap reviews, intake, and release communications.
* Coordinate with peer product managers on shared data, instrumentation, integration points, and sequencing so analytics reflect the full product ecosystem.
* Define and track KPIs such as analytics adoption, self-service usage, time to insight, data quality, reduced manual reporting, and client satisfaction.
* Bring structure to ambiguity, using both quantitative data and qualitative feedback to make decisions and influence without direct authority.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Kubernetes Accelerated Runtime
jobs.desc:
Running GPU-accelerated Kubernetes reliably is deceptively hard. A small change to a driver, kernel, operator, or Kubernetes version can break a cluster in ways that are painful to diagnose and expensive to reproduce. AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) is NVIDIA's open source project to define a validated, reproducible software stack that can go into every AI cluster, published as version-locked recipes customers can trust through end-to-end supply-chain provenance.

NVIDIA is hiring a product manager to lead the accelerated runtime that defines every GPU Kubernetes cluster. You'll set the direction for the NVIDIA AICR project and grow it into how the industry runs NVIDIA's software stack on Kubernetes, growing its coverage across accelerators, clouds, and workloads. The role also represents AICR to customers, partners, and the open-source community. Want to bring GPU infrastructure to life and power NVIDIA innovation? We'd love to hear from you!

What we need to see:

The mission is ambitious: make NVIDIA's accelerated software stack the runtime that powers every GPU Kubernetes cluster! This role will:

•
Own AICR and related technologies, set product direction, and standardize how customers and partners run NVIDIA's GPU software stack on Kubernetes.

•
Expand coverage across accelerators, clouds, and workloads, from training and inference to agentic AI.

•
Keep the stack current and trustworthy, turning NVIDIA's validation into recipes that customers can deploy with supply-chain confidence.

•
Represent AICR and other NVIDIA projects to customers and partners, and lead their growth in the open-source community.

What We Need to See:

We're looking for an experienced product manager who can go deep on GPU infrastructure and lead an open-source project in the open.

•
12+ years in technical product management across cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, or developer and platform tooling.

•
A bachelor's or master's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent experience.

•
Depth in the Kubernetes GPU stack: cluster provisioning and lifecycle, operators and drivers, scheduling, and the compatibility failure modes across kernel, driver, OS, and Kubernetes versions.

•
Experience with GitOps and cluster configuration delivery (Helm, Argo CD, Flux, or equivalent tools) and the realities of shipping configuration that has to be reproducible.

•
A track record of contributing to open-source projects, including community strategy and external presence such as conference talks or technical writing.

Ways to Stand Out from the crowd:

We're especially interested in candidates who also bring experience:

•
Hands-on work with NVIDIA GPU infrastructure, DGX systems, the GPU Operator, or GPU-aware Kubernetes scheduling.

•
Software supply-chain security: SLSA, SBOMs, Sigstore or Cosign, or reproducible builds.

•
Packaging and distributing a sophisticated software stack (operators, drivers, platform components) across clouds and hardware.

•
Owning or contributing to a widely adopted cloud-native or CNCF open-source project.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Card Schemes
jobs.desc:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 676,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,300 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

About the team

The Product team at Airwallex is a group of passionate builders and problem-solvers who are obsessed with crafting customer-centric solutions that empower businesses to operate anywhere, anytime. We combine technical expertise with a deep understanding of our customers' needs to design and build unified, intuitive, and scalable products. As a team, we thrive in a collaborative and fast-paced environment, constantly iterating and pushing boundaries to deliver exceptional product experiences.

What you’ll do

This role will be part of the payments product team, building out our capabilities that enable businesses to collect credit card payments and other forms of payments on their website or app from consumers around the world. You’ll be working on the payment lifecycle end to end, from connections with the card schemes, authorizations, captures, refunds, and reconciliation.

Responsibilities:

You will be responsible for leading high-impact projects from ideation to launch on topics such as:

•
Expanding our coverage of card schemes and markets to provide merchants globally the ability to acquire payments of all major card brands

•
Optimizing the competitiveness of our card payments infrastructure through adoption of new industry standards and working closely with our machine learning team to increase the success rate of payments

•
Building stable foundations for our payment infrastructure to scale with our business growth, reducing internal manual efforts and minimizing the risk for any service interruptions for our merchants

Who you are

We're looking for people who meet the minimum qualifications for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory.

Minimum qualifications:

•
8+ years of professional experience, ideally with exposure to a high-growth environment

•
Bachelor's degree or above with a competitive GPA, preferably with engineering or computer science coursework

Preferred qualifications:

•
Deep expertise in payment processing, working on direct integrations with Visa and MasterCard (preferably on acquiring side)

•
Solid technical understanding and ability to engage in architectural discussions with engineering teams

•
Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey product strategy to both technical and non-technical audiences

•
Close attention to detail, ability to structure complex problems and inform decisions with data and first-principle insights

•
Drive, grit, and persistence are necessary to take ownership and move ideas to reality in short periods of time

•
Ability to thrive in cross-cultural and cross-functional team

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through ca

Director of Product Management, Commerce Billing

The HubSpot Product team is passionate about building tools that help businesses market, sell, serve their customers, and ultimately grow better. They are able to work autonomously, lead with psychological safety, and grow a team into more than the sum of its parts.

jobs.title: Director of Product, CX Product
jobs.desc:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 75,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 1 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About This Role:

Every month, hundreds of thousands of patients and providers interact with Headway's support systems. Today, most interactions are handled by human agents working across disconnected tools. We believe CX is a product, not just a department — and the right product leader can transform how Headway supports its customers while dramatically improving both satisfaction and cost efficiency.

As Director of Product for CX, you will build Headway's CX product function from the ground up. You'll own the product vision and strategy for how patients and providers get help — from AI-powered self-resolution to context-aware agent tooling to the feedback loops that connect support insights back to the product.

You will:

  • Define the vision and strategy for Headway's CX product — spanning AI-powered resolution, agent tooling, proactive engagement, channel strategy, knowledge systems, and the feedback loops that connect support insights back to the product.
  • Build and lead a team of product managers focused on reducing cost-to-serve while increasing resolution quality and customer satisfaction.
  • Own the AI resolution layer — build the agentic workflows and API integrations that enable the AI agent to actually resolve problems, not just answer questions. Define the autonomy framework: what AI handles without human involvement, what needs guardrails, and what requires a human.

jobs.title: Director, Product Management - Nemotron
jobs.desc:
Open large language models (LLMs) are unlocking exciting new capabilities. Developing, training, and deploying these models requires both technical expertise and domain-specific knowledge. They power applications in data centers and at the edge, including automobiles, drones, and medical devices. As their agentic capabilities expand, so does the need to identify and mitigate potential risks. NVIDIA is at the forefront of advancing research and delivering product innovations for the broader AI community!

As the Nemotron Product Manager for Model Risk, you will lead key areas of NVIDIA's model risk management portfolio, addressing frontier challenges in cybersecurity, content moderation, data protection, and more. Nemotron makes model checkpoints, datasets, and training techniques available to the community to help minimize risk and broaden adoption. You will define model safety requirements and evaluations, partnering with research and engineering teams to reduce harmful outputs and improve model robustness. You will also engage with customers to define products and roadmaps, develop business strategy and market positioning, and bring products to market. We need a self-starter to grow this area and help build the future of AI.!

What you'll be doing:

• Enterprise Model Risk Management: Define requirements for model evaluations and mitigations, such as post training improvements and guardrails

• Contribute to Open Source: Publish and guide the community on best practices for identifying and mitigating open model risks.

• Define and Prove: Collect insights and build market analysis that provides the data to enter or change new markets through a clear value proposition for the product

• Market intelligence: Understand the developers, partners, and competitors

• Build and Deliver: Collaborate with engineering to promote the customer's needs through setting feature priorities across roadmaps

• Sense and Respond: Work closely with customers, build surveys, present at conferences, understand product quality and supervise critical bugs

• Marketing content creation: Work with marketing to define positioning that enables the creation of technical content, including blog posts, webinars, developer tutorials, and more to communicate the product value proposition

• Product launches: Define the go-to-market strategy and provide mentorship to the cross-functional implementation of the plan across marketing, public relations, and sales.

What we need to see:

• BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or other technical field (or equivalent experience). MBA is a plus.

• 15+ overall years of technical product management, or similar, experience at a technology company

• 6+ years direct people management experience.

• Passion for delivering software, libraries and SDKs

• Proven track record of teamwork across teams, customers, and partners

• Outstanding interpersonal and public communication skills with a shown ability to articulate a value proposition to technical and non-technical audiences

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Background working with Large Language Models, specifically with setting evaluation tasks as well as curating data, training or fine-tuning, to increase model capabilities

• Experience with enterprise AI safety, responsible AI, or model risk management.

​NVIDIA is widely considered one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the world's most forward-thinking and hardworking people on our team. . As you plan your future, see what we can offer to you and your family www.nvidiabenefits.com/

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 272,000 USD - 425,500 USD.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until October 11, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.title: Director, Product Management – AI Networking Spectrum HW
jobs.desc:
NVIDIA’s Datacenter Ethernet Business is growing rapidly. We are seeking a Director-level Product Manager with deep technical expertise in networking hardware, silicon, and platform architecture to lead global product strategy for next-generation Ethernet networking solutions. This senior leadership role offers broad cross-functional collaboration, executive visibility, and global responsibility for shaping NVIDIA’s intelligent networking portfolio.

As a product management leader, you will define the long-term strategy and drive the lifecycle of advanced networking hardware and silicon platforms, working closely with architecture, ASIC, systems, software, and go-to-market teams worldwide. Positioned at the intersection of AI infrastructure, high-performance networking, and cloud-scale datacenter innovation, you will influence the direction of NVIDIA’s next-generation networking technologies and help shape the future of accelerated computing.

What You’ll Be Doing:

•
Lead the strategic direction and product vision for NVIDIA’s Ethernet networking hardware and silicon platforms, driving product planning, execution, lifecycle management, and technology transitions.

•
Define product requirements and roadmaps for next-generation networking ASICs, systems, and platforms in collaboration with engineering, architecture, and key ecosystem partners.

•
Drive cross-functional execution across hardware, silicon, firmware, software, operations, and business teams to deliver industry-leading networking solutions for AI and cloud datacenters.

•
Partner with strategic customers and hyperscalers to understand emerging requirements and translate them into differentiated networking products.

•
Represent the product strategy with executive leadership, customers, and industry partners, influencing the evolution of NVIDIA’s datacenter networking portfolio.

What We Need to See:

•
BS/MS in Engineering or equivalent experience.

•
15+ years of overall experience with 8+ years in software or infrastructure roles within the networking industry, with deep technical proficiency.

•
Deep knowledge of Ethernet switch and router hardware, including switching/routing ASICs, packet-processing pipelines, and the underlying silicon that powers modern data center networks.

•
Solid grounding in data center hardware, rack-level build, and physical infrastructure is required. This includes server, networking, power, cooling, and cabling considerations that develop how AI and cloud fabrics are deployed at scale.

•
Experience leading product strategy development and delivery in complex global organizations as a senior IC (director-level scope) or people leader.

•

jobs.desc:
Head of Product | Contract, 20 hrs/week to start, growing into full-time | Remote (US overlapping hours) | Reports to the CEO

The short version

Koast is the AI operating layer for teams that run Meta ads at volume. Agencies, in-house media buying teams, and enterprise buyers managing 10+ ad accounts and launching 50+ ads a week use Koast to launch faster, automate optimizations off real attribution data, and see every account from one hub. The Koast Agent is the next layer: an AI that reads the account, spots what matters, and acts inside guardrails.

We are a small team shipping fast. The product is live, customers are paying, a Whop partnership just onboarded a wave of new users, and the Agent build is underway. What we do not have is one person who owns the product end to end: what gets built, why, in what order, and whether it actually landed.

That is this role. It starts at 20 hours a week on contract. If you are the right person, it becomes the full-time product seat at Koast.

What you will own

Discovery that finds the real problem. You will sit in on enterprise sales calls and onboarding sessions, run discovery with agencies and media buying teams, and figure out what they are actually trying to get done versus what they say they want. Every feature request gets mapped to a job: launching smoother, getting their team in, getting tasks done, keeping users active and growing spend inside Koast. If it does not serve a job, it does not get built.

Specs that engineering can execute without a meeting. We run a lean engineering team plus an AI-assisted dev pipeline. That only works when the ticket is unambiguous. You will write PRDs and Shortcut tickets that define the behavior, the edge cases, the data dependencies (Meta API limits, Hyros and Cometly attribution feeds, Whop account provisioning), and the acceptance criteria. If an engineer or an agent has to guess, the spec was not done.

The queue, and what is missing from it. You own the Up Next column. You will keep engineering fed so they are never blocked, and you will keep a standing view of what is discussed in Slack, support, and QA that does not yet have a ticket. Gaps are your problem before they become customer problems.

Evidence over opinion. PostHog, Intercom, session replays, rage clicks, support threads. You will run the user-behavior audit, know where people drop off in launching, and bring numbers to every prioritization argument, including the ones with the CEO.

Delivery from spec to shipped. Governance, milestones, release notes, and the customer conversation after it ships. When something breaks or slips, you are the one who says so early, not the one who explains it after.

Technical judgement in a non-deterministic product. The Koast Agent makes decisions off data that is noisy, seasonal, and shaped by Meta's learning phase. You will make product calls that respect that: what the Agent is allowed to do, what it must never do, how we measure whether an automated action was correct. Guardrails are infrastructure here, not UI. You need to understand why.

  • Run discovery sessions with prospects and customers and turn them into scoped, execution-ready PRDs.

Using software tools and thoughtful product design, we've been able to safely reduce incarceration and improve outcomes. We work side-by-side with leaders of the criminal justice system, people in prison and on supervision, and ecosystem partners to build a better path forward. People who succeed at Recidiviz lead with kindness and humility, assume good intent, learn from failure, and fix problems when they see them. **Director, Product Management (PrintOps)**  
**Pharos | US Remote**

  
  
*Here's what you'd actually be stepping into: an established product, two new markets it hasn't reached yet, and no one left who can tell you why it behaves the way it does. Some people need that explanation handed to them. Others go dig it up themselves. This role is for the second kind.*

### About Pharos

Pharos Systems International is the leader in PrintOps, the integrated, user-centric, and cloud-native approach to managing printing and the infrastructure and operations behind it. Pharos' modern print management software empowers enterprises to reduce costs, strengthen security, and support today's hybrid workforce with simple, reliable, and scalable printing solutions. Trusted by thousands of organizations, including many of the world's largest Fortune 500 companies, Pharos has helped eliminate print servers, cut millions in print-related spend, and accelerate the transition to cloud-based infrastructure. Headquartered in Rochester, NY, Pharos has been delivering innovative print management solutions and measurable ROI since 1992.  
  
Our flagship product already runs inside a large, established customer base, which means it carries real history, real workarounds, and a level of hidden complexity that isn't written down anywhere. We're also pushing it into new markets it hasn't served before, without losing the trust of the customers who already rely on it every day. That combination, protecting what works while extending what's possible, is exactly why this role exists.

### What This Role Is

This role owns the full product loop for one of Pharos's most established product areas: understanding how it actually works today, bringing its capabilities under control, deciding what to build and what to explicitly leave alone, and making sure Engineering and the rest of the company are working from the same understanding you are.  
  
You'll work directly with enterprise customers, including the conversations where the answer is no, and you'll set direction across customer commitments, technical constraints, and two new markets at once, without letting the loudest voice in the room decide the roadmap for you.  
  
You'll also use AI as a normal part of how you work: discovery, synthesis, competitive research, epic drafting, documentation, not as a novelty, but as how the work actually gets done, in a fast loop with Engineering that doesn't wait on oversized specs.

### What You Will Own

* The model of how this product actually works, and keeping it current as you learn more.
* A visible roadmap where every item has a reason, an owner, and a real answer for what Pharos is and isn't doing.
* The path from a raw signal (a support ticket, a sales request, a customer complaint) to a decision someone can act on.
* Direct conversations with enterprise customers, including the ones where the answer is no.
* The translation of product direction into work Engineering can actually build and verify against.
* Making sure Sales, Support, Customer Success, Services, and Marketing know what changed and why, not just that it changed.

### What a Strong Background Looks Like

* You've owned a mature, complicated product, one with real history, real workarounds, and a real customer base, not just a green-field build.
* You've sat across the table from enterprise customers directly: discovery calls, pilots, advisory relationships, the uncomfortable ones included.
* You've turned a messy customer or market need into something Engineering could actually build against, and stuck around to see what happened after.
* You've made a complex product simpler, more consistent, or easier to reason about, not just added more to it.
* You reach for AI as a normal part of how you think through a problem, not as a novelty.

**Strong fit if…**

  

You're looking to build and lead a team starting now.  
You've only ever built new products from a blank sheet,

jobs.title: Director, Product Management (Security)
jobs.desc:
**Director, Product Management (Security)**  
**Pharos | US Remote**

  
  
*Here's what you'd actually be walking into: one early customer, a real thesis, and everything else still unproven. Some people need the market validated before they'll commit to building in it. Others want to be the one who proves it's real. This role is for the second kind.*

### About Pharos

Pharos Systems International is the leader in PrintOps, the integrated, user-centric, and cloud-native approach to managing printing and the infrastructure and operations behind it. Pharos' modern print management software empowers enterprises to reduce costs, strengthen security, and support today's hybrid workforce with simple, reliable, and scalable printing solutions. Trusted by thousands of organizations, including many of the world's largest Fortune 500 companies, Pharos has helped eliminate print servers, cut millions in print-related spend, and accelerate the transition to cloud-based infrastructure. Headquartered in Rochester, NY, Pharos has been delivering innovative print management solutions and measurable ROI since 1992.  
  
Pharos has an early proof of concept in security and real conviction about where the market is headed. What we don't have yet is proof it holds up at scale, or a repeatable way to turn that thesis into a validated business. That gap is exactly why this role exists.

### What This Role Is

This role owns the full loop from thesis to revenue: understanding who the real buyer is and what they'll actually pay to solve, turning an existing proof of concept into something multiple customers can rely on, and building the go-to-market motion that gets it from a handful of pilots to a repeatable business.  
  
You'll work directly with Engineering, not just direct it: prototyping, reviewing technical tradeoffs, and getting into implementation details yourself when that's the fastest way to learn something. You'll also work directly with customers and, over time, with Sales, to turn early proof into paying accounts.  
  
You'll report directly to the CEO, with the autonomy that comes with that and the visibility too. There's no team here yet. What you build, you build largely with your own judgment and your own hands.

### What You Will Own

* The market thesis: who the real buyer is, what they're actually willing to pay for, and what this product will deliberately not attempt.
* The path from an early proof of concept to something multiple paying customers can rely on.
* Direct, hands-on work with Engineering: epics, prototypes, requirements, and implementation tradeoffs.
* The go-to-market motion: positioning, packaging, pricing input, and what it takes to turn a pilot into a paying customer.
* A fast, honest read on what's working and what isn't, reported straight to the CEO, without waiting for a perfect plan to have that conversation.

### What a Strong Background Looks Like

* You've built and shipped something close to zero to one, not just contributed to an already-mature product line.
* You've worked directly with customers to test whether a problem is real and worth paying to solve, not just gathered requirements secondhand.
* You've gotten into the technical details yourself: a prototype, a proof of concept, a spec you wrote and then helped build.
* You've made a real call with incomplete information and lived with the outcome, good or bad.
* You reach for AI as a normal part of how you think through a problem, not as a novelty.

**Not a good fit if…**

**Strong fit if…**

  

You need a validated market and an established team in place before you're willing to commit to a direction.

You're comfortable being the person who validates the market, not just executing inside one someone else already proved.

  

Your best work has come from directing others rather than building things yourself.

You still want to be hands-on with prototypes and implementation, not just strategy.

### What We Offer

* Compensation: $165,000 - $170

Head of Product Management for Quantum Modalities, Quantum Technology Solutions
  
Quantum Technology Solution (QTS) is the new business recently launched at GlobalFoundries to enable the Quantum industry to transition from lab-scale to Utility Scale Quantum Computing
  
The Head of Product Management for Quantum Compute Platforms is responsible for defining and commercializing GlobalFoundries' portfolio of modality-specific quantum computing platforms. This leader will own the business, develop the product strategy, roadmap, and go-to-market plans for photonic, ion trap, neutral atom, and other emerging quantum computing modalities.
  
Working closely with strategic customers, ecosystem partners, and QTS process development team, the role translates customer requirements into scalable semiconductor manufacturing platforms and technology roadmaps. The successful candidate will help establish GF as the leading foundry partner for utility-scale quantum computing by developing differentiated process technologies, integration flows, and product offerings that accelerate the transition from research prototypes to manufacturable quantum systems. This role is ideal for an experienced business executive with a strong background in product management of new technology platforms incl. photonics, quantum modalities and advanced packaging platforms.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Own the business growth and profitability, product strategy and roadmap for GF's quantum compute platform portfolio, with primary focus on photonic, ion trap, and neutral atom quantum computing platforms.
* Develop modality-specific product offerings including process technologies, integration flows, design enablement, and manufacturing solutions required to scale quantum processors.
* Engage with quantum computing customers to understand architecture roadmaps, technical requirements, and commercialization needs.
* Translate customer requirements into market requirements, platform specifications, and technology development priorities for QTS development team.
* Drive go-to-market strategy, business cases, ecosystem partnerships, and strategic customer engagements to accelerate adoption of GF quantum platforms.
* Monitor industry trends, competitive developments, and emerging quantum modalities to guide portfolio investment decisions.

* Advanced degree in Physics, Electrical Engineering, Photonics, Materials Science, Quantum Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
* 15+ years of experience in product management, strategic marketing, business leadership, or technology commercialization within semiconductors, photonics, advanced packaging, or quantum technologies.
* P&L ownership, and demonstrated success launching and scaling complex technology platforms from concept through commercialization.

* Strong customer-facing and executive communication skills

SmithRx is a rapidly growing, venture-backed Health-Tech company. Our mission is to disrupt the expensive and inefficient Pharmacy Benefit Management (PBM) sector by building a next-generation drug acquisition platform driven by cutting edge technology, innovative cost saving tools, and best-in-class customer service. With hundreds of thousands of members onboarded since 2016, SmithRx has a solution that is resonating with clients all across the country.

We pride ourselves for our mission-driven and collaborative culture that inspires our employees to do their best work. We believe that the U.S healthcare system is in need of transformation, and we come to work each day dedicated to making that change a reality. At our core, we are guided by our company values:

* **Integrity:** Our purpose guides our actions and gives us confidence in the path ahead. With unwavering honesty and dependability, we embrace the pressure of challenging the old and exemplify ethical leadership to create the new.
* **Courage:** We face continuous challenges with grit and resilience. We embrace the discomfort of the unknown by balancing autonomy with empathy, and ownership with vulnerability. We boldly challenge the status quo to keep moving forward—always.
* **Together:** The success of SmithRx reflects the strength of our partnerships and the commitment of our team. Our shared values bind us together and make us one. When one falls, we all fall; when one rises, we all rise.

**Job Summary:**

  

We are looking for a strategic and visionary Leader of Product Marketing who will be responsible for leading our overall go-to-market strategy, product positioning, and sales enablement efforts. SmithRx isn't just building another technology platform; we are rebuilding the pharmacy benefits category from the ground up. In this highly cross-functional leadership role, you will define how we communicate the radical value of SmithRx's platform to brokers, employers, consultants, and members, establishing us as the clear alternative to the broken status quo.

You will be responsible for building, mentoring, and scaling a high-performing product marketing team, bringing complex new capabilities to market, and driving greater adoption of our products and services. As we expand our platform capabilities, a critical part of this role will be navigating the narrative around Artificial Intelligence in healthcare. You will lead the charge in educating our market, building trust around our AI-powered features, and demonstrating how these technologies improve outcomes.

To be successful in this role, you should demonstrate a strong track record of scaling PMM functions, driving category creation, translating complex and emerging technologies into compelling stories, and partnering closely with executive leadership across Product and Sales. You must be comfortable operating in an unstructured, fast-paced environment and learning as you experiment.

About LoopMe

LoopMe is an AI company solving one of advertising's hardest problems: making brand advertising actually measurable — and making it perform. Our platform runs patented machine learning models across billions of consumer signals in real time, optimising campaigns toward outcomes like purchase intent, brand lift, and foot traffic rather than proxy metrics like clicks. The result is 2–5x better performance than industry benchmarks, at scale.

We operate a high-load programmatic infrastructure — processing millions of ad requests per second with sub-200ms response times globally. This isn't a layer on top of someone else's stack; it's built from the ground up, in-house, by the team you'd be joining. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in London, we now have 400+ people across 19 cities and have sustained 40% revenue CAGR since 2018. The engineering problems here are real, the ownership is genuine, and the scale is significant.

The opportunity

LoopMe connects direct SDK and web supply with leading DSPs across performance, commerce, and brand advertising. As Director, Product Management, Demand, you own the product capabilities that make these partnerships more valuable and easier to scale. You work closely with DSP partners to shape the roadmap, build solutions together, and turn marketplace insight into products that grow demand revenue. You report to the Chief Product Officer.

What you'll do

* Own the demand product strategy and roadmap, turning Performance, Commerce, and Brand playbooks into priorities across creative, signals, inventory access, bidder health, and measurement.
* Partner with DSP product and technical teams to understand their buying goals and constraints, and co-build capabilities that improve results for their advertisers.
* Define flexible, repeatable integration capabilities across the Chartboost and LoopMe exchanges, so partners launch faster and gain wider access to supply.
* Drive performance and commerce spend with products that help DSPs find valuable users and inventory, optimize bidding, and deliver stronger advertiser results.
* Establish consistent definitions and reporting for bid requests, QPS, impressions, CTR, and other funnel metrics, so partners and internal teams can act quickly.
* Measure the impact of each product on partner adoption, campaign performance, and revenue.
* Lead delivery from partner insight to launch with Engineering, Ops, BD, and partner teams, with clear tradeoffs, clear ownership, and measurable results.

What you'll bring

**Essential:**

* 8+ years of product management in programmatic advertising, including time on an ad exchange, SSP, or DSP.
* Experience owning product strategy and a roadmap for a revenue-generating area, and measuring features against revenue impact.
* Deep knowledge of OpenRTB and DSP integrations, including bid requests, QPS, signals, and deal setup.
* Established relationships with DSP product and technical teams, and experience co-building products with external partners.
* Experience leading cross-functional work with Engineering, Ops, and BD, making clear tradeoffs and shipping high-quality products.

**Nice to have:**

* Experience managing and developing product managers.
* Experience with mobile in-app SDK supply and performance or commerce advertising.
* Experience standardizing integrations across many demand or supply partners.
* Experience defining marketplace metrics and reporting used by partners and internal teams.

What we offer

* Self-managed vacation (no maximum)

* LoopMe Gives Back
* Learning & development support, including internal mobility and bi-annual promotion cycles

Compensation

$150,000-$200,000

### **About Us**

Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.

We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process.

### **About the Role**

Twitch is looking for a **Director, Head of Product Marketing** to build, lead, and elevate our global PMM function from the ground up. Reporting directly to the Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), your mandate is to establish Product Marketing as a proactive, high-velocity marketing engine and strategic driver.

In this role, you will define the core value proposition of Twitch’s product ecosystem for creators and viewers alike. You will act as the crucial connective tissue between Marketing and teams across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Commerce and the broader Go-To-Market teams. You understand that the best marketing on a platform feels like a feature, not a bug. You’ll build systems that move beyond one-off "launch day hype,” anchoring your strategy in continuous lifecycle adoption and creator unit economics. You’ll ensure that our community understands the deep *why* behind our tools before the *what* even ships.

You can work in San Francisco, CA; Irvine, CA; New York, NY; or Seattle, WA.

### **You Will:**

* **Architect the Global PMM Discipline:** Lead, coach, and scale a world-class team of product marketers, establishing operational rigor, written strategy briefs and clear accountability loops that prioritize high-impact bets over busywork.
* **Define the Value Translation for Creators:** Translate complex technical roadmaps and platform mechanics into transparent, compelling creator value narratives. Demonstrate how Twitch’s breadth of monetization tools can be a meaningful driver of creator earnings, giving creators more ways to build income.
* **Partner on the Core Discovery & Product Roadmap:** Act as a strategic peer to Product, Design, and Engineering leadership to help solve platform-wide discovery challenges.
* **Bridge Product to Partnerships & BD:** Partner closely with teams across the business to ensure new platform features, onboarding pathways, and retention mechanics directly recruitment and retention goals.
* **Champion Data-Backed Market & Audience Insights**: Unearth deep audience affinities and user research to help the platform bridge the gap between our core gaming foundation and expanding lifestyle, sports, and creative verticals.
* **Turn Marketing into a Native Platform Feature**: Ensure that every user-facing message, in-product promo, and CRM touchpoint delivers immediate community value and respects the sacred relationship between streamers and their viewers

### **You Have:**

jobs.desc:
**Director of Product**  
Team: Product  
Reports to: McKay Ferrell, CPO  
Location: Remote, United States  
Type: Full-time  
  
Job Summary  
As a Director of Product at SureCost, you'll own the business of a set of products that pharmacies  
depend on to keep drugs on the shelf at the right cost. You'll bring new products to market and make  
our existing products better, from the first customer conversation through launch and adoption. You'll  
know our customers well enough to build things they love to use, and you'll measure whether they do.  
This is a hands-on role. You'll talk to customers every week, prototype ideas before engineering builds  
them, and work with our commercial team to launch and sell what we ship. We're rebuilding how our  
product team works around AI tools, and you'll help shape that as you go.  
  
Essential Functions  

* Own the roadmap, outcomes and quarterly priorities for your product areas, and decide which

initiatives make the quarter within the capacity your pods actually have.  

* Run a monthly business review for your area covering adoption, customer issues, revenue signals

and delivery against plan.  

* Build toward product-level P&L visibility for your area with the CPO.
* Own the quality of what your area ships, including the share of engineering time that goes to various

initiatives.  

* Build and help guide product builder team members with AI tooling and structures.
* Stay close to customers. Expect several customer conversations a week, including the hard ones

with enterprise accounts.  

* Work with the commercial team on product launch planning and enablement, including launch

timing, sales training, demo readiness and customer communication.  

* Partner with Marketing on positioning, messaging and competitive intelligence for your products.
* Give pricing and packaging input for new products and major enhancements.
* Bring what you hear from Sales, Customer Success and the market back into the roadmap, including

win/loss patterns and competitor moves.  

* Track adoption after launch and work with Customer Success to drive it.
* Build and ship prototypes, skills and agents yourself, and set the standard your team follows for AI-

assisted discovery, specs and evaluation.  

* Own the AI agents in your area end to end: the problem they solve, the precision bar they have to

meet, the evaluation that proves it, and where a named human approves an action.  

* Recommend when to stop or reshape an initiative, and bring the evidence.

SureCost | Job Description  

* Work across product areas with the other Director, Product Ops and Design so the product lifecycle

(inventory, purchasing, shortage) holds together for the customer.  
  
How We Work  

* Product areas own the work. Our value streams point where our teams are focused and set how

each pod's hours are split, and every Director plans inside that split.  

* Our product builders combine what used to be PM, PO and UX roles. Agents draft stories,

acceptance criteria, status and first-pass triage. People make the decisions and own the quality.  

* AI fluency is part of how we hire and how we review.
* We're remote-first. Most of our work takes place over digital ecosystems, including video calls,

chats, email, and other systems – you’ll need to be self-motivated and comfortable in an all-remote  
environment.  

* The domain is complicated: GPO contracts, wholesaler operations, DSCSA, 340B and drug shortages.

We give you time to learn it, and we expect you to go deep.  
  
Requirements  

* 5+ years in product management for B2B or enterprise SaaS, including 2+ years leading product

managers or product owners.  

* Bachelor’s degree or higher in Business, Pharmacology, or related required.
* A record of owning product outcomes, such as adoption, retention or revenue, and being able to

show what changed because of your decisions.  

* Hands-on AI fluency you can demonstrate: you've built prototypes, workflows
