**ABOUT LEMONTREE**
-------------------

There are more food pantries in the US than there are McDonalds, but most families facing hunger don't take that help. That's why we started Lemontree–because it makes no sense for our neighbors to go hungry when there's free food around the corner. We've helped one million households access the free food in their communities by bringing technology + empathy to the experience of food assistance. Learn more about us at https://www.foodhelpline.org/about.

### **Our Values**

**Service Over Self**

We put the mission — helping people find food — ahead of ego, credit, or agenda. That means caring for the people we serve and the team around us, and going the extra mile when it makes a real difference. We're here for the work itself and what it makes possible for others.

**Ownership**

We get shit done and we carry our piece so the whole team can move forward. When we make a mistake, we name it early and openly, because a problem we've owned out loud is one we can fix together. In a growing org, this kind of autonomy & accountability is how we do big things with a small team.

**Curiosity**  
We don't take anything for granted. We stay curious about our users and ourselves. We stay humble enough to accept that there's always room to improve. We stay ready to change course when the evidence points somewhere new. The plan we have today is a strong draft, but we'll always need to adapt to a changing world. We'd rather ask the better question and adjust than defend a stale answer.

**THE POSITION**
----------------

Lemontree is looking for a **Head of Product** **& Technology** that will partner with the Executive Director to own and evolve our platform strategy to scale our impact. Since 2020, we've grown from a simple helpline into a platform that serves thousands of families, partners, and volunteers daily. What we need now is someone who can shepherd us to the next level, bringing rigor and direction to how we evolve: sharper prioritization, better use of our data, and clearer decision-making & process around where we invest our resources. Every decision we make should align with our strategic anchors:

* User-centered

* Hospitality in every interaction

* Built for scale

This is a hands-on leadership role with high trust and high agency, reporting to the Executive Director. You'll be the person setting product direction and leading the charge to move it forward, partnering with an engineering agency on execution and collaborating closely across our broader Lemontree team. While product ownership is the focus, this is a multi-disciplinary position that combines product management, data analysis, and technical leadership to build toward stability *and* scalability. If you like operating with real autonomy and are motivated to take things from 1 100, this role will suit you.

### **What You'll Do**

Drive **technical leadership** that delivers a reliable, joyful, scalable user experience for neighbors looking for food assistance.

* Serve as a credible technical voice in conversations about architecture, tradeoffs, and feasibility.
* Direct our engineering agency, translating product priorities into well-scoped technical work and holding a high bar for what ships.
* Oversee third party services that support our product, including setting up integrations, managing billing, negotiating nonprofit discounts, etc.

Own a **product roadmap** that increases the breadth & depth of our impact, aligned with our organizational strategy.

* Partner with CEO & senior leadership to shape overall strategy & product direction. Rather than making every single product decision, you will own the process that helps those decisions happen with the right information, clear accountability, and strong follow-through.

**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Enterprise security is one of the fastest-growing and most strategic areas at Amazon Web Services (AWS), and we are looking for a marketing leader to own how the world understands it. As the leader of Product Marketing for AWS Security and Identity, you will set the marketing strategy for a high-growth business, define the category narrative, and build the team that brings it to life. In this role, you will sit at the center of how AWS establishes itself as a leader in enterprise security.
  
  
This is a rare chance to own a strategic business end to end from a product-marketing standpoint. You will decide where to invest, what story to tell, and how to measure whether it is working, while partnering with engineering, finance, go-to-market, and sales leaders to generate growth. You will be building the team that will drive the growth, including hiring, developing, and shaping a team of product marketers into a group known for sharp storytelling, strong business judgment, and deep technical credibility with security buyers.  
  
If you are a product marketing leader who wants the autonomy to shape a category, the scope of a business that matters, and the opportunity to build a team you are proud of, this role is for you.

Own the product marketing strategy for the AWS Security and Identity portfolio, and set the category narrative that positions AWS as a leader in enterprise security.
  
  
Own positioning, messaging, and launch strategy across the portfolio, and represent AWS with customers, at industry events, and in analyst and executive interactions.
  
  
Partner with the Security and Identity product leaders to shape the portfolio roadmap based on working back from customer needs.
  
  
Decide where to invest for the greatest return, using data and customer insight to guide strategy, prioritization, and the initiatives the team designs and launches.
  
  
Set the bar for how the team measures impact, and build the habit of testing ideas, learning quickly, and deciding with evidence.

Smarsh empowers its customers to manage risk and unleash intelligence in their digital communications. Our growing community of over 6500 organizations in regulated industries counts on Smarsh every day to help them spot compliance, legal or reputational risks in 80+ communication channels before those risks become regulatory fines or headlines. This specific role assumes full product leadership for an entire suite of products serving the SMB (small and mid-sized businesses) segment which is a huge growth area for Smarsh. * Own and manage relationships with key external partners — industry analysts, press, and technology partners — relevant to the product portfolio
* Represent Smarsh in partner, analyst, and customer forums to build market credibility and inform product strategy

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world. World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached. Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you. About the role *Preferable to have someone near one of our offices in NYC or San Francisco, but open to hiring around the world for the right candidate. Runway Enterprise is a complete solution for enterprises, offering out-of-the-box creative tools, a generative media developer platform, model licensing, and forward-deployed creatives and researchers that embed directly within enterprises. We're hiring an Enterprise product marketing leader for Runway Enterprise, leading the segment and developing priority verticals including Media, Retail/eCommerce, Software, and more. This is not a purely positioning or “launch” role. You'll own the success of the enterprise segment, partnering closely with the sales & enablement team, enterprise marketing & growth. You’ll lead the development of Runway’s overall enterprise messaging and positioning and create tailored, vertical-specific messages and value propositions, built from your first-hand experiences engaging directly with Runway’s customers. This is a builder's role. You'll be defining the discipline, working shoulder-to-shoulder with sales, product, creative, marketing and growth; you'll be measured on the growth of the business (not just on assets shipped or messaging consistency). Robertshaw is a global design, engineering, and manufacturing company serving the appliance, automotive, and commercial markets. The company develops and manufactures controls and related products for applications including cooking, refrigeration, laundry, water heating, heating, and automotive and commercial systems. Headquartered in Itasca, Illinois, Robertshaw has more than 4,000 employees across 9 countries.

**Position Summary**

Robertshaw is seeking a Senior Director, Product Management to lead the global Product Management organization for its Gas and Water Valve product lines.

Reporting to the Chief Commercial Officer, this role will own product strategy, portfolio direction, market development, and commercial performance for these businesses. The Senior Director will lead a global Product Management team and work closely with Sales, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Finance to drive profitable growth, strengthen the portfolio, and develop the next generation of products.

This is a hands-on leadership role. The successful candidate will set strategy while remaining directly involved with key customers, product roadmaps, competitive analysis, business cases, pricing, and major product development initiatives.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead global product strategy and portfolio management for Robertshaw's **gas and water valve product lines**.
* Develop product roadmaps based on customer needs, market trends, competitive dynamics, technology, and growth opportunities.
* Identify opportunities to grow the business through new products, applications, customers, and adjacent markets.
* Manage product portfolio performance, including revenue, margin, pricing, product costs, and investment priorities.
* Work directly with key customers and Sales to understand market needs and develop commercial opportunities.
* Partner with Engineering to prioritize product development and ensure resources are focused on the highest-value opportunities.
* Work with Operations and Supply Chain on product cost, manufacturing strategy, capacity, and footprint.
* Lead cross-functional teams through product development, commercialization, and lifecycle management.
* Establish effective Product Management processes and develop a strong global team.
* Evaluate portfolio opportunities to reduce unnecessary customization and complexity while increasing differentiated products and platforms.
* Personally lead critical customer, product, and strategic initiatives when hands-on involvement is required.

**Qualifications**

* Approximately 12 years of progressive experience in Product Management, Engineering, Business Development, Sales, or related technical/commercial roles.
* **Direct experience with gas valves and/or water valves is required**, preferably in appliance, HVAC, water heating, or related industrial applications.
* Demonstrated experience developing product strategy and leading global teams.
* Proven commercial track record with responsibility for product growth, profitability, pricing, or portfolio performance.
* Experience working directly with OEM customers and understanding their product development and purchasing processes.

We're hiring one product person, posted at two levels: Founding Product Manager and Head of Product. Apply to the one that fits you best. This is an individual contributor role.

**About Klarify**
-----------------

Backed by Y Combinator, with $1.7M in funding, Klarify helps more than 13,000 therapists every day with their notes and their practice.

Therapists train for years to help people, then spend their evenings writing notes, marketing their practice and chasing insurance. Klarify does that work for them, so they can spend their time on clients. Therapists write to tell us it gave them time back with their families.

Moody (CEO) started Klarify after therapy changed his life, and after his own therapist asked to use the note-taker he was building.

**The product and vision**
--------------------------

Today, therapists use Klarify to:

* Turn a session into a draft clinical note
* Ask Klara, our AI assistant, questions about their sessions, or have it draft a letter or treatment plan
* See a visual map of the themes across a client's sessions
* Get found by new clients through profiles and blog posts built for Google and ChatGPT

Notes were the start. We're building one place that runs the whole business side of a therapy practice: notes, marketing, billing, insurance and admin. We want to automate everything a therapist does except the therapy itself.

**The role**
------------

You'd join Moody (CEO), Bergie (CTO) and Zach (founding engineer) as our first product leader. You'll own product strategy and work directly with the CEO on where the product goes next. Therapists have full caseloads and little time to learn new software, so the best version of every feature is the simplest one.

* Own product strategy and the roadmap. Decide where we focus, in what order and what we say no to.
* Design the platform as it grows. Plan how notes, Klara, marketing, billing and insurance fit together, and how we package and price them.
* Set how product works here: how we decide what to build, write specs, test before we ship and measure what worked.
* Work with the CTO on what gets built when. You make the trade-offs between new features and fixing what we have.
* Set the product targets for adoption, retention and revenue per customer, and report on them.
* Stay close to customers. Talk to therapists every week, own support and turn what you hear into fixes.
* Build privacy into every product decision, working with the CTO, who owns security and compliance (SOC 2, HIPAA, PIPEDA, PHIPA and Quebec's Law 25).
* Help the CEO tell the product story to investors as we head toward our Series A.
* Ship code yourself: prototypes, internal tools and pull requests with Claude Code, plus flows designed with AI tools and whatever else the company needs.

Your first project: set the next six months of the roadmap, starting with getting more therapists to use what we've already built.

The CEO owns the company's direction and approves what we build next and why. The rest of product is yours.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------

* 7+ years of product management experience, including at least 2 leading product at a startup or as part of a founding team
* You've set a product strategy and owned the results, good and bad
* You've designed how a growing product fits together, including packaging and pricing
* You've worked side by side with a CEO and an engineering lead to decide what to build
* You're AI native. You use AI tools every day and have brought them into how your team builds product.
* You have an eye for UX and can make complicated things feel simple
* You ship code. You've opened pull requests that made it to production, with Claude Code or a similar tool. This is a must.
* You're authorized to work in the US or Canada. We can't sponsor a visa right now.
* Strongly preferred: you're in San Francisco and can work hybrid
* Nice to have: you've worked in healthcare, mental health or another regulated industry

At Office Ally, we've been revolutionizing healthcare administration since our inception. What started as a clearinghouse focused on simplifying insurance claims processing for healthcare providers has grown into a full-suite healthcare technology company. AIAEC is hiring a Head of Product to lead the strategy, development, commercialization and growth of our SaaS portfolio: current and future products.

**Commercialization & Adoption**

**About Volley**
================

Volley Automation is building the future of parking through fully automated robotic parking systems. Our mission is to create sustainable parking solutions that are compact, efficient, and adaptable throughout a building’s lifecycle, while making EV charging easier and more accessible.

Are you intrigued by the idea of putting cars away with robots? Do you hate parking? Do you love parking? If so, we’d love to talk.

Volley Automation builds fully automated parking. Drivers hand off their car at the entry bay and walk away. From there the building takes over: AGVs move vehicles on trays, vertical conveyors move them between floors, and a controls and software stack orchestrates everything. The result is a garage that fits more cars into less concrete, in exactly the urban cores where parking is most expensive to build. Our systems go into real buildings, on real construction schedules, with real occupancy dates. That constraint shapes everything about how we build, develop, and engineer our product.

**The Role**
------------

* Turn customer and market evidence into product decisions: segment definition, configuration and pricing structure, feature go/no-go. Evidence means site visits, operator and owner interviews, and win/loss definitions and not a survey deck someone else built
* Articulate a product vision and get a company that does not yet agree to align behind it, in front of the executive team, the board, customers, and all the way through the entire org - especially the engineering team. You have held the line against per-project one-offs quietly becoming the product

* Experience with a product where the buyer and the user are different people with different definitions of value (developer and owner on one side, driver or parking spot owner/user on the other)

* Owns a cross-functional development roadmap and plan spanning engineering, operations, commercial, and finance with time estimates that are aggressive and still real. Experience delivering this roadmap against an externally fixed date (construction schedule, customer opening, capital project milestone), where the date does not move because a certain department needs or wants it to
* Runs dependency mapping, critical path, and a risk register as habits, with suppliers, contract manufacturers, integrators, and long-lead components tracked as schedule dependencies
* Can close the loop from our Denver HQ and field deployments by turning commissioning, operational friction, and customer feedback into requirements and backlog items

**Required qualifications**
---------------------------

* 8+ years combined, with real depth on both sides of the product owner and program execution fronts. At least 3 years owning a product and at least 3 years owning a program outcome, which may overlap
* Experience with product definition and/or technical program execution with AGVs, AMRs, robotics, material handling, warehouse automation, or vertical transportation

* Hire, develop, and set priorities for the Product Marketing Engineers. Give them the access and authority to investigate important technical questions and turn their findings into proof, launch and adoption guidance, and specific product feedback.
* Own Temporal's technology ecosystem strategy. Decide which partner categories and integrations matter, set the portfolio narrative, and coordinate joint launches with Product, Engineering, Business Development, the Product Marketing Engineers, and the Solutions and GTM Director.
* Meet customers regularly at least 3 to 4 customers per month.
* Regularly supporting strategic sales deals and collaborating with key sales stakeholders.
* Make clear tradeoffs. Decide which launches need a full company motion, which need focused technical communication, and which do not need a launch at all.

**What You Will Bring**
-----------------------

* Significant product marketing experience with developer tools, cloud infrastructure, open-source software, distributed systems, data infrastructure, or another deeply technical product.

DigiCert is a global leader in intelligent trust. We protect the digital world by ensuring the security, privacy, and authenticity of every interaction. Our AI-powered DigiCert ONE platform unifies PKI, DNS, and certificate lifecycle management, to secure infrastructure, software, devices, messages, AI content and agents. Learn why more than 100,000 organizations, including 90% of the Fortune 500, choose DigiCert to stop today's threats and prepare for a quantum-safe future at www.digicert.com

**Job summary**

AI agents are moving from experimentation into production—accessing enterprise data, invoking tools, writing code, and acting on behalf of people and organizations. As they become more autonomous, enterprises need a new trust layer: one that establishes who an agent is, who owns it, what it is authorized to do, and how that authority can be revoked. DigiCert is building that trust layer. DigiCert AI Trust Manager extends our foundation in digital identity and cryptographic trust to AI agents, models, and the agentic ecosystem—letting organizations discover AI assets, establish verifiable identities, govern access through policy, monitor activity, and revoke authority when trust conditions change. We are looking for a Head of AI Product Management to build this business from the ground up: an entrepreneurial leader who thrives in ambiguity, has taken emerging technology to scale, and can operate across AI, security, identity, and enterprise infrastructure. You will define not only what we build, but the category we create around it.

**Build the product and category**

* Own the vision, strategy, roadmap, and execution for DigiCert's AI Trust portfolio.
* Turn a fast-moving AI ecosystem into clear customer problems, product bets, and differentiated capabilities—including opportunities that have no established market category yet.
* Develop strong points of view on how identity, authorization, policy, provenance, attestation, and cryptographic trust must evolve for AI agents and models.

**Scale**

* Operate like a founder inside DigiCert: move quickly from customer problem to hypothesis, prototype, validation, and repeatable offering.
* Engage design partners and early customers directly to understand their AI architectures, security challenges, and buying criteria.
* Know when to experiment, when to iterate, and when to scale—balancing speed with the security and reliability enterprise infrastructure demands.

* You do not need to write production code, but you should be technical enough to prototype, evaluate architectures, challenge assumptions, and earn the trust of highly technical teams.

jobs.title: Director, Product Management
jobs.desc:
**Company Description**

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

 **Job Description**

***Who*** **We're Looking For:**

We are looking for a Director of Product Management to lead a team of PMs as well as own the product strategy for empowering developers on the Now platform to build and take their applications to production faster. These areas include developer reach, testing, sandboxing, metering, and deployment of AI and human generated code.

As agentic build tools compress the time it takes to author a change, the bottleneck moves downstream. Testing and deploying safely to production is already one of the loudest customer asks and one of the sharpest pain points on the platform. When changes originate from agents as well as people, and arrive at a much higher rate, the ability to validate and trust them quickly stops being a quality-of-life improvement and becomes a precondition for platform growth. You will lead the team that enables this for developers.

This is not four adjacent feature areas with a shared manager. Customers experience the SDLC as one motion, and the central product challenge of this role is the connective tissue: a sandbox that behaves like the instance you will deploy to, a test suite that knows what changed, a release path that carries the evidence, and a model for building directly in production that an admin can actually govern. You set the strategy that makes their roadmaps resolve into a single lifecycle rather than four products that ship past each other.

The scope is deeply technical and close to execution. The Developer Reach feature area alone unlocks a path to building in production that admins can manage at scale without losing control, and it demands real technical depth to steer. You will also carry a broad surface, over twenty product areas, with the escalation volume that comes with it, and you will need to run that operational load without letting it consume the strategic work.

**What you get to do in this role:**

* Own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap across Developer Reach, Developer Sandboxes, Agentic Testing, and Release Ops, and define how they compose into one lifecycle from authored change to governed, audited deployment.
* Build, lead, and develop a team of PMs, one per area. Set a clear standard for product craft, coach PMs on strategy and execution, and hold the bar on the seams between them: shared primitives, consistent models, and a single coherent customer narrative.
* Set product direction for validating AI-originated change at scale: what it means to trust an agent's output, what evidence a release needs to carry, and how much of the test and review burden can be automated without losing accountability.
* Drive the Developer Reach strategy, including the product model for building in production with admin control, guardrails, and reversibility at enterprise scale.
* Define the sandbox strategy: provisioning speed, production parity, data handling, and the developer experience of getting a safe place to work in seconds rather than days.
* Own the release governance path end to end, including the tradeoffs between developer velocity and auditability, and the gating model that makes those tradeoffs explicit rather than accidental.
* Shape the metering and cost-modeling strategy for this area in partnership with Pricing & Packaging and Finance, and underst

jobs.title: Vice President of Product
jobs.desc:
**About Onfleet**

Onfleet is the last-mile delivery platform behind millions of deliveries every month for thousands of businesses around the world. We enable shippers to manage deliveries across their private fleet, carriers, and couriers. We make it easy for dispatchers to plan and run their operations, drivers to execute deliveries, and recipients to get real-time tracking and notifications. Our customers span grocery, prepared meals, pharmacy, flowers, furniture, and more.

### **The Role**

We're looking for a **Vice President of Product** to lead Product at Onfleet, owning how our strategy gets translated into roadmaps and how roadmaps turn into shipped, adopted products. Your job is to sharpen our strategy where needed and define how the Onfleet product suite evolves as we scale up in a fast-growing market. This is a hands-on leadership seat where you'll stay close to the details and roll up your sleeves when the team needs it.

You'll report to our CEO and lead Product Management, Design, and User Research. You’ll also work closely with Engineering, QA, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Experience. As our senior-most product leader, you'll sit on our Strategic Leadership Team and represent Product in company planning.

### **What You'll Do**

* Own the product roadmap that delivers on our strategy, and update both as our market and target customers change.
* Prioritize aggressively by committing to a few well-scoped bets per quarter and saying no to other competing initiatives.
* Build deep knowledge of the last-mile delivery industry and our core users: shippers, carriers and couriers, dispatchers, drivers, and recipients.
* Lead quarterly and annual planning with Engineering and go-to-market leaders, and partner with them to set company goals that tie product work to business outcomes.
* Own how we gather, prioritize, and close the loop on product feedback from customers, Sales, CX, and other internal teams.
* Coordinate work across squads so dependencies and risks surface early, and keep one roadmap view the whole company can see.
* Connect product success metrics to company metrics, and build a team habit of defining success before launch and acting on what adoption data shows.
* Represent Product internally and with our board of directors, customer advisory boards, and key customers.
* Foster a collaborative team culture and think ahead about team structure, process, and tooling.
* Coach the team and define clear growth paths for each member.

### **What You'll Bring**

* You have 10+ years in B2B SaaS product roles, including 5+ years leading product teams and 3+ years as Director of Product or above.
* You've run Product at a Series B+ company generating tens of millions of dollars in ARR.
* You've led a product through a move upmarket into enterprise.
* You've directly hired, managed, and developed Product Managers, Designers, and User Researchers.
* You have significant UX and design experience, and you champion it across the company. You've overseen teams that run usability tests, user interviews, and experiments.
* You've partnered with Engineering as equals: scoping work together before committing, keeping scope stable once work starts, and shipping in small iterations.
* You've run market research to size opportunities in a customer base and adjacent markets.
* You make roadmap calls by weighing customer evidence, usage data, strategy, and business impact, and you explain the trade-offs clearly.
* You're analytical, using data to make decisions and hold yourself and your team to the numbers.
* You've built or managed a Product Operations function, with working fluency in tools like Jira, Productboard, and Amplitude.
* You communicate clearly in writing and in person.
* You're highly organized and focused on outcomes.

### **Nice To Have**

* Experience in last-mile logistics or delivery.

### **What We Offer**

* Remote-first work environment with quarterly domestic travel
* Generous employee stock options

**The role**
------------

The Director of Product, Pay owns the product experience and technology-enabled workflows that move a purchase through payment, invoice processing, and reconciliation. You will lead product strategy, discovery, definition, delivery, instrumentation, and post-launch improvement for Pay, working with Engineering and Design and in close partnership with the Payments business leader and Finance.

**The role**
------------

The Director of Product, Buy owns the buying experience and the product decisions that shape marketplace economics. This is the pillar closest to where customers experience value every day: finding the right product, at the right price, from the right supplier, and knowing what happens after the order is placed.

Catalog quality, supplier coverage, sourcing intelligence, and fulfillment reliability shape both the customer experience and the cost of serving it. You will lead product work across those levers, partner closely with Marketplace and vendor operations, and measure the contribution of Buy product changes to purchasing volume, margin, and cost-to-serve.

You will establish clear PM ownership across catalog and search, sourcing and fulfillment, and the vendor network, building and developing a team as staffing and delivery capacity permit. You will be accountable for defined outcomes, not a backlog.

**What you will own**

### **The buying experience**

* Catalog, search, and product discovery, including how customers find what they need and how we guide them toward better choices.
* Sourcing and substitution: presenting alternatives on price, availability, and delivery speed, and making the better choice the easy one.
* Cart construction, order placement, and the pre-purchase journey.
* Fulfillment and order tracking, including how we communicate delays, exceptions, and partial shipments.
* The experience across multi-location customers, where a regional manager, a site lead, and a central procurement team may need different views of the same activity.

### **Marketplace economics and cost-to-serve**

* Catalog coverage and quality across customer needs, including how we prioritize which gaps to close.
* Product levers that influence marketplace margin, including sourcing, substitution, catalog quality, and the cost of fulfilling orders.
* Product and automation changes that reduce supplier onboarding effort and cost per supplier, with Marketplace and vendor operations.
* Product improvements to manual vendor workflows, portal automation, and exception handling. Measure their contribution to lower operating cost with the operational owner; this role does not own the vendor-operations team or its entire budget.

### **Vendor commerce integration**

* Product strategy and requirements for order transmission, supplier portals, catalog feeds, and EDI connections to vendors, in partnership with Engineering and vendor operations.
* The product decisions that make orders reach suppliers reliably and at scale.
* Partnership with Engineering on which integrations to build, automate, improve, or retire.

jobs.desc:
Stash exists to put a financial advisor in everyone's pocket: investing, banking, and personalized guidance in one app for everyday Americans to invest and save with confidence.

Stash is hiring a **Director of Product** to lead Engagement; the in-app experiences that help people decide what to invest in, how much to put in, and what to do next.

You will lead the product managers on Engagement, on web and mobile. You will be accountable for whether subscribers use the product and stay: product usage, recurring contributions, and retained paying subscribers. You will report to the Head of Product and partner as a peer with Design, Engineering, Marketing, Data, and Compliance.

This is a player/coach role that is best for someone that wants to manage and develop people while staying hands on. You'll set the strategy, manage 2-3 Product Managers, and lead by example as part of a team yourself.

* Set multi-quarter strategy for Engagement: guidance, investing and banking surfaces, and the habits that keep subscribers active

* Own the Engagement roadmap across web and mobile, and decide what gets capacity when the team is pulled in more than one direction
* Hold the team to outcomes: product usage, recurring engagement, and retained paying subscribers
* Partner with Marketing so lifecycle messaging and the in-app experience tell one story
* Run a rhythm of discovery, experimentation, and shipping inside regulatory guardrails
* Represent Engagement in leadership forums with a clear story and numbers
* Use AI in how you and your team do the work, and expect the same from the people you hire

* 10+ years in product management, including several years managing product managers
* Strong consumer app experience: you have owned a mobile and/or web product people use in daily life, and you can talk about user and business impact with numbers

* You can set strategy and still get into the details when a decision depends on them
* Clear communication with executives, peers, and your team
* A strong partner to engineering, design, marketing, and data
* You use AI in your workflow today, or you are ready to adopt it here and with your team
* Strong experimentation practice and fluency with product analytics (Mixpanel, Looker, or similar)

**Gold Stars**

**About Us**
  
If your goal is to build a career that makes a difference, consider joining the dedicated people of the Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS). Our professionals strive to design and deliver high quality human and health services that improve the safety, independence, and well-being of the people of Colorado. In addition to a great location and rewarding and meaningful work, we offer:

**Description of Job**
----------------------

**CoBEES what is it?**

The Colorado Benefits Eligibility and Enrollment Systems (CoBEES) is a cross-agency portfolio of information technology systems, subsystems, applications, interfaces, training, and communications managed and maintained by the State of Colorado to deliver access to public assistance and medical coverage programs for Coloradans. The CoBEES portfolio includes the Colorado Benefits Management System (CBMS), Program Eligibility and Application Kit (PEAK), PEAK Pro, Electronic Document Management System (EDMS), MyColorado Benefits, and the Joint Agency Interoperability (JAI) program. CoBEES supports multiple state departments—operating through a collaborative governance and product operating model between the Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS) and the Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing (HCPF)—to administer critical state benefits such as Medicaid, Child Health Plan Plus (CHP+), SNAP, WIC, and TANF. The principal users of these systems include county benefit eligibility technicians, state program administrators, and program participants across Colorado.

  
  
  
  
**What will you be doing?**
  
  
The Head of Product (HOP) serves as the executive product and portfolio leader for the CoBEES portfolio, establishing and executing the technology and product vision for the systems that enable county workers to administer public benefits to Coloradans. Leading a joint CDHS-HCPF-CDEC-OIT product management organization, the HOP oversees day-to-day product ownership of systems including CBMS, PEAK, and Joint Agency Interoperability (JAI). This position works in close partnership with CDHS’s Business, Innovation, Technology, Security Division (BITS), HCPF’s Health Information Office (HIO), the Governor’s Office of Information Technology (OIT), and contracted vendor partners to ensure CoBEES technologies support end users while advancing product management maturity and best practices across the portfolio. This position provides direct supervisory oversight of the CBMS, PEAK, and JAI product teams and serves as a collaborative executive partner with senior leaders across both departments, including HCPF’s Medicaid Chief Operations Officer and Deputy Director of the Health Information Office, as well as CDHS’s Office Director for Economic Security and Office Director of Infrastructure, to ensure coordinated governance and strategic direction of CoBEES. The HOP serves as the day-to-day executive accountable for the CoBEES portfolio. Housed within CDHS, the position reports directly to the CDHS Deputy Executive Director of Community Partnerships (who serves as the appointing authority) and a dotted line reporting relationship with the Health Information Office (HIO) Deputy Director at HCPF. The HOP maintains joint accountability to the Executive Directors of both CDHS and HCPF. jobs.desc:
Courier Health is on a mission to solve one of the biggest and most meaningful opportunities in healthcare: reinvent how people living with chronic and rare diseases are supported.

We are building the future of patient engagement for life sciences companies. Our software is leveraged by biopharma companies to support patients in their complex journey from diagnosis to initiating and remaining on therapy to achieve optimal health outcomes.

### **Come Build with Us**

We're a NYC-based team that believes culture, craft, and customer obsession go hand in hand. We show up for each other the same way we show up for the people we serve. We're an office-first company that values in-person collaboration 4 days per week because we believe the best work happens when you can collaborate and brainstorm together in the same room. If that sounds like your kind of place, we think you'll love it here.

### **The Opportunity**

Courier Health is at an inflection point. We exist to get patients faster, better access to life-saving therapies, and product helps to shape decisions related to which patients we reach next and how soon.

As Director of Product, you will lead a team of product managers covering the full platform, reporting directly to the CEO. You will also keep a hand in the work running discovery, writing the spec, making the call — on the bets that matter most.

The roadmap here is not handed down. You will decide what we build, in what order, and what we deliberately don't do, in a market where the right answer is rarely obvious and the stakes are patients starting therapy. If you have led product teams inside someone else's operating model and want to define your own, this is the seat.

### **What You'll Build**

**A product team that makes its own calls.** You will coach to a standard in weekly one on ones and roadmap reviews, raise the bar on writing and discovery, and give your PMs enough room to be wrong and get better. The goal is a team that can size a bet and defend it without you in the room.

**A roadmap the whole company can bet on.** Sales, implementation, and engineering all plan against what product says is coming. You will set the sequencing across a growing customer base, make the tradeoffs between what one strategic client needs and what the platform needs, and say no clearly enough that people trust the yes. Commitments hold, and when they change, everyone knows why in time to act.

**Discovery grounded in how patients actually get to therapy.** Our users are the people running patient support programs, field teams, and hub operations. You will get your team in front of them, translate what you hear into product, and build the customer and market fluency that makes our roadmap hard to copy. Strong opinions are welcome here. Strong opinions without customer contact are not.

### **What Makes You Successful**

* 10+ years in product management at a B2B software company, with a track record of shipping products enterprise customers renewed and expanded.
* 5+ years managing product managers. You have hired, coached, and given hard feedback that made someone better.
* Proven ownership of a roadmap end to end from customer discovery and strategy through launch and measured outcomes, not just execution against someone else's plan.
* Strong technical fluency. You can work through data models, API integrations, and architectural tradeoffs with engineers and hold your own. Coding is not required. Depth is.
* Excellent judgment under ambiguity. You can make a call with incomplete information, explain the reasoning, and change course without drama when the evidence shifts.
* Exceptional written communication. You think in documents, and your specs make the decision obvious.
* Comfortable working directly with senior customer stakeholders, including the conversations nobody wants to have.
* Experience building process where none existed, and the restraint to keep it minimal.

jobs.title: Head of Product / Lead Instructor
jobs.desc:
**ABOUT TECHBOOTCAMP.COM**

TechBootcamp.com is an online career education company. We are starting with the Data Center Accelerator, which helps U.S. tradespeople, veterans and suitable career changers transition into data center roles.

**THE ROLE**

We are hiring a senior Head of Product / Lead Instructor to build the program from the ground up and own its development, delivery and improvement.

This is a leadership role. You will be responsible for the complete learning product and the team that supports our students, and you will work directly with the founder on strategy, priorities and resources.

**WHAT YOU WILL DO**

* Define the program structure, target roles, entry requirements and learning pathways, and own the roadmap from build through expansion.

* Design the full learning journey, including shared foundations and role-specific pathways, with lessons, exercises, assessments and career preparation.

* Develop realistic practice scenarios, projects and a capstone with clear rubrics, and evaluate licensed and custom simulations.

* Hire, onboard, train and manage coaches, instructors and specialist contributors.

* Set the educational requirements for the app, LMS, AI assistance, labs and progress tracking, and work with designers and developers.

* Serve as lead instructor, teach and record core material, and set the teaching standard.

* Keep content current, track student progress and employment outcomes, and keep improving the product.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

* Current or recent experience in data center operations, critical facilities or a closely related technical leadership role, with deep expertise in at least one discipline.

* Experience creating, launching or materially improving a technical training program, academy or training operation.

* Experience hiring, training, managing and developing a team.

* A track record of developing technicians or other technical learners, and confidence teaching on camera.

* Good product and execution judgment across subject-matter experts, content teams and developers.

* Knowledge of U.S. data center roles and hiring expectations, including the difference between IT operations and facilities pathways.

* Sound judgment on technical and safety standards, including the difference between simulated practice and verified physical competence.

**COMPENSATION**

Six-figure annual base salary plus a performance bonus.

Remote | U.S.-based preferred.

Pay: $100,000.00 - $180,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule
* Paid time off

Work Location: Remote

jobs.desc:
**About Bruno**
===============

Bruno is the local-first, Git-native API client trusted by more than 4 million developers worldwide. From startups to Fortune 500 companies, engineering teams use Bruno to build, test, and collaborate on APIs without the complexity, cost, or security concerns of cloud-first tools.

We're building beyond the API client, expanding into API collaboration, documentation, registries, and enterprise developer workflows.

We have a product developers already love, a passionate open-source community, and an ambitious roadmap. We're looking for someone to help define what comes next.

**About the Role**
==================

We're looking for a product leader who is still a builder at heart.

Someone who has strong opinions about what makes a great developer product, understands the technical details behind it, and enjoys working closely with engineers to bring ideas to life.

You'll lead Bruno's product direction, work closely with the founders and engineering leadership, and develop a growing team of Product Managers.

This isn't a role for someone who wants to manage roadmaps from a distance. We want someone comfortable opening the product, reproducing bugs, talking to developers, challenging assumptions, writing specifications, and getting into the weeds with engineering.

You'll need to balance the needs of our open-source community, individual developers, and enterprise customers while keeping Bruno simple, focused, and enjoyable to use.

We value strong opinions, but we expect them to be challenged. You'll need the judgment to make difficult trade-offs, the curiosity to understand problems firsthand, and the ability to turn ambitious ideas into products that actually ship.

**What You'll Do**
==================

* Own product strategy and roadmap: define where Bruno should go, what we should build, and equally importantly, what we should not build.
* Set a high bar for product quality, developer experience, usability, simplicity, and craftsmanship.
* Lead and develop the PM team: coach Product Managers, improve product thinking, and build a team capable of independently owning meaningful product areas.
* Stay close to developers: regularly engage with users, understand their workflows, and identify problems worth solving.
* Partner deeply with Engineering to work through technical trade-offs, architecture, feasibility, and scope.
* Turn ambiguity into clear product decisions, specifications, priorities, and measurable outcomes.
* Balance long-term product bets with consistent execution and delivery.
* Use product analytics, customer feedback, market understanding, and judgment to make informed decisions.
* Partner with Sales and Marketing to understand customer needs, support product-led growth, and inform pricing and packaging decisions.
* Work directly with the founders to challenge assumptions, align on priorities, and build a strong product culture.

**What We're Looking For**
==========================

* 7+ years of Product Management experience, preferably in developer tools, infrastructure, or technical platforms.
* Strong technical depth across APIs, Git, networking, developer workflows, and system architecture.
* Exceptional product judgment and a strong instinct for simplicity and developer experience.
* A builder's mindset: you enjoy prototyping, experimenting, and getting hands-on with products.
* A proven track record of taking meaningful products from idea to launch, with measurable results.
* Deep developer empathy and a genuine understanding of how developers work.
* Strong prioritization skills and the conviction to say no to ideas that don't move the product forward.
* Excellent written communication and the ability to bring clarity to ambiguous problems.
* Opinionated but low-ego, comfortable challenging ideas and changing your mind when the evidence warrants it.
* Experience leading and mentoring Product Managers while raising the quality of product thinking.

jobs.title: Director of Product Marketing
jobs.desc:
Oligo is a fast-growing cybersecurity startup transforming how organizations protect their applications, cloud environments, and AI systems at runtime. Backed by top-tier investors including Greenfield Partners, Red Dot Capital Partners, Lightspeed, Ballistic Ventures, and TLV Partners, we're on a mission to make real-time security a reality.

Oligo's industry's leading runtime security platform built to stop attacks in real time without stopping the business. We transform security from passive visibility to active protection across applications, cloud services, workloads, and AI systems. By uncovering the deepest layers of what actually runs in production, Oligo helps organizations prioritize exploitable vulnerabilities, detect malicious behavior as it happens, and stop modern attacks in their tracks.

We're looking for a **Director of Product Marketing** to own Oligo’s story end to end- from market positioning and differentiation across our product lines (runtime protection/ADR, AI security, and runtime vulnerability management) to equipping our GTM teams to win.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll lead a small team while staying close to the work: crafting messaging, building launch plans, and presenting to customers and sellers.

Product Marketing sits within Product Management at Oligo. You'll partner daily with PMs on roadmap and launches, and work closely with Sales, Marketing, and leadership on pipeline generation and enablement. You'll connect what we build with how the market understands its value.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Lead the Function**

* Own positioning, messaging, and narrative across Oligo’s product lines, ensuring consistency as the product evolves.
* Define the product marketing roadmap and priorities, aligned with product development and GTM goals.
* Lead, coach, and develop a small team of product marketers.
* Represent Product Marketing in cross-functional planning, bringing market insights and competitive intelligence into roadmap decisions.

**Drive Execution**

* Product launches & campaigns: Lead end-to-end GTM for new products and features, from positioning and messaging to launch plans, sales enablement, and integrated campaigns.
* Market & competitive intelligence: Track competitors across ADR, CNAPP, EDR, AppSec, and AI security, translating insights into positioning and product recommendations.
* GTM enablement: Equip Sales, SEs, and partners with the training and tools they need to win, including battlecards, one-pagers, pitch decks, demo narratives, and ROI models.
* Content & storytelling: Create product-led content across blogs, product tours, videos, launch assets, conferences, and analyst materials, ensuring consistent messaging across channels.

  
Requirements:  
  

**Qualifications**

* 6+ years of Product Marketing experience in cybersecurity, including 2+ years leading or mentoring product marketers. Runtime security experience is a plus.
* Proven track record of launching technical software products and driving adoption of new capabilities.
* Strong technical acumen, with the ability to engage with engineers and security practitioners, understand detection architectures, and translate technical concepts into clear business value.
* Exceptional writing, storytelling, and presentation skills, with the ability to make complex technical products compelling and relevant to buyers.
* Strong understanding of enterprise software buyer journeys and complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles.
* Analytical mindset, with the ability to turn data and market insights into actionable recommendations.
* Creative, energetic, and collaborative, with the ability to influence without authority and thrive in the ambiguity of a fast-growing company.

**Nice to Have**

* Experience in runtime protection, application security, cloud security, or detection and response (ADR, CNAPP, EDR, WAF).
* Experience working at a company defining or entering a new market category.

jobs.title: Head of Product - Interfaces
jobs.desc:
In the early 1980s at Bell Labs, Gerald Ash and his colleagues questioned a rule that AT&T's long-distance network had followed for decades; a call climbed a fixed hierarchy of switches until it found an open path. They modeled the idea, simulated it, and tested it until it held. In 1984, AT&T put Dynamic Nonhierarchical Routing (DNHR) into the national network, which became the basis of global real-time telephony routing that came after it.

At Mercury, customers reach us through Dashboard, Mobile, Command, our API, and Model Context Protocol (MCP). Each request should take the best path to the work, whatever surface it starts on. We're looking for a Head of Product, Interfaces to design that network. You'll set one direction across these surfaces and lead the PMs who build them. You'll also build the shared capabilities that let every Mercury team reach customers well: navigation, tasks, notifications, and agent interactions. AI is central to the role. The job is to find where AI removes real work, and to make it dependable enough to trust with money.

This is a hands-on leadership role reporting to the VP of Product. You’ll develop people while staying close to customers, prototypes, product decisions, and shipped quality.

* *Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.*

* Connect the portfolio across Mercury. Partner with teams building banking\*, Spend, Books, Payroll, and other products to bring their capabilities into shared experiences

jobs.title: Director of Product — SafeSend (Gather & Deliver)
jobs.desc:
**Director of Product — SafeSend (Gather & Deliver)**

**Job Description:**

Accounting firms are reinventing how they prepare tax returns, and their clients, taxpayers expect a simple, secure, digital way to hand over documents and get a finished return. Firms expect everything in between to be faster, more automated, and connected to the tools they already run. SafeSend is where that happens: the taxpayer-facing perimeter and engine of Tax Workflow for accounting firm clients, the surface taxpayers touch, and, through its APIs, the engine firms build their own workflows on.

As Director of Product for SafeSend, you will own that surface and lead its evolution into an AI-driven, agentic gather-prepare-deliver experience on Thomson Reuters’ CoCounsel platform and open it up so firms and partners can build on it.

**The opportunity:**

* Firms are consolidating fragmented point tools into one connected workflow and want a single partner to deliver it.
* Taxpayers expect a modern, mobile, trustworthy way to share documents and receive their return.
* Document data extraction is going AI-native; firms want agentic preparation and review and are adopting it now.
* Firms increasingly want to build on open APIs so their own portals, data and reporting stay connected as the market converges.
SafeSend sits at the center of all four. This is a build-and-converge mandate — shaping a market-defining product, not maintaining a mature one.  

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Deliver SafeSend. Own the SafeSend portfolio end to end — Gather, Organizers, e-Sign, Delivery, Returns and Extensions — season over season, at the reliability and scale that tax-filing peaks demand.
* Converge SafeSend and TaxCaddy. Bring the best of SafeSend and TaxCaddy together into one Gather & Deliver experience for every firm and taxpayer[CH1]
* Componentize the portfolio. Turn each part of SafeSend into reusable workflow components that can be recomposed across the gather – prepare – deliver flow and used across the broader CoCounsel platform, rather than locked inside a single app.
* Enable expanded SafeSend access via APIs and orchestration. Expand the SafeSend API surface — open APIs, events and integrations — as a first-class capability, so firms and partners embed SafeSend in their own portals and workflows and keep their tools, data and reporting connected, with orchestration so AI agents and partner systems can coordinate gather and delivery programmatically.
Deliver agentic Gather & Deliver through CoCounsel. Bring agentic Gather — and AI-driven extraction, preparation and review — into the SafeSend experience on the CoCounsel platform, so more of the work shifts from staff to the platform while the firm stays in control.  

**What success looks like:**

* Firms experience one connected Gather & Deliver workflow, whatever ecosystem they run today.
* The SafeSend API is something firms and partners actively build on, not a bespoke integration project.
* Firms reach AI-driven, agentic preparation and review through SafeSend, season over season.
Taxpayers get a simpler, faster, more trustworthy experience — and firms see measurably less manual work.  

**Required Qualifications:**

* 8+ years in product management, including leading a product line at scale as a Director or senior PM.
* Experience building and productizing platform, API or developer-facing products — not only features on top of them.
* A track record of converging or migrating products without disrupting existing customers.
* Fluency with AI-native products (data extraction, agents, orchestration) and comfort partnering with a platform team.
* Strong systems thinking — able to see a portfolio as composable components rather than a monolith.
* Experience in the tax & accounting workflow space strongly preferred
Strong stakeholder management and a proven record of building high-performing teams  

  

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Background in tax & accounting, fintech, or document / data-pro

jobs.title: Head of Product Led Growth
jobs.desc:
**About Re:Build**
------------------

At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.

We operate a sophisticated, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.

The way we operate is as meaningful as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and give to the communities where we operate. The Re:Build Way principles

Re:Build is building Livewire, a launchpad business bringing AI-native software to intuitive wire harness design and manufacturing. The product is real, customers are already using it, and there's still a lot to learn about how the growth engine should work; that's where this role comes in.

We're looking for a hands-on product growth leader who can connect the whole customer journey: how the right users find Livewire, what gets them into the product, what gets them to real value, what brings them back, and what eventually gets them to pay. You'll work closely with Product and also partner with Marketing, Sales, RevOps, and Customer Success. Together, you will make that journey measurable and keep a consistent flow of experiments. These experiments will help turn what you learn into better product and growth decisions.

This is a builder role. You should be just as comfortable looking at product behavior as acquisition data, enjoy running experiments, want to talk to users, and be energized by the fact that there isn't a mature growth playbook waiting for you — because you'll help build it. You'll likely start with few or no direct reports. Instead, you will guide external firms, contractors, and internal specialists. See that as an opportunity rather than a limitation.

**What You Get To Do**
----------------------

* Own the growth journey from acquisition through activation, lifecycle and conversion.
* Build a clear view of the customer journey; who's converting, where they get stuck, and whether they're reaching real value.
* Run a steady cadence of experiments across acquisition, onboarding, product experience, lifecycle and conversion.
* Partner with Product to turn user insights into a faster path to value.
* Build the measurement and operating rhythm that helps the team learn and decide faster.
* Drive conversion, retention and expansion with Sales, RevOps and Customer Success.
* Shape positioning and messaging based on customer insight, in partnership with Marketing.
* Direct agencies and specialists to move faster, without outsourcing the thinking.

**What You Bring To The Team**
------------------------------

* Experience in product growth, PLG, lifecycle marketing or a similar role; and you know growth doesn't stop at signup.
* Hands-on experience designing and running experiments, including with imperfect data and small samples.
* Strong partnership with Product, using customer and product data to drive decisions.
* Comfort operating with high autonomy and limited infrastructure.
* Strong quantitative skills funnels, cohorts, conversion and experiment analysis.
* Familiarity with product analytics, CRM/marketing automation, web analytics and experimentation tools.
* Preferred: product-led, self-service or digital commerce experience. Wire harness/CAD/manufacturing expertise not required.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Product-led, self-service, digital commerce or online buying experience.
* Domain expertise in wire harnesses, CAD

jobs.desc:
**What We Are Building**

BigTime is a PSA platform for professional services firms. Thousands of consulting, IT services, and engineering firms run their business on it. We are now building our next-generation platform from the ground up, AI-native from the first line of code.

What we are going after is an autonomous back office, where agents run the whole chain from quote to cash. Scoping and pricing the work, staffing it, capturing time and expense, recognizing the revenue, getting the invoice out, and chasing the payment. Firms do all of that by hand today, stitched across half a dozen tools that do not talk to each other. Nobody in this market has built the chain end to end, and we have something a newer competitor cannot go out and buy: years of project history from thousands of firms to build against.

If we get this right, these firms stop running their back office and start supervising it. That is the thing you would be leading.

**The Role**

You will lead our product management team, and most of your time goes to the new platform. The roadmap, the release sequencing, the scope decisions, and the PMs who own each piece of it. It is the biggest investment the company has made and the board follows it closely.

You will also own the roadmap for BigTime Delivery, the platform our existing customers use today. It is the smaller part of the job and a dedicated team runs the day to day. What we need from you is the judgment on what gets fixed, in what order, and when we stop.

**What You Will Own**

* The roadmap. What ships in which release, what gets cut, which customers migrate when, and the written case for all of it. Priority gets argued from pipeline data, product usage, customer research, and win and loss analysis, rather than whoever asks most often.
* The product management team. Hiring, coaching, and the standard for the work.
* Specifications. We use spec-driven development, so the spec feeds the agentic build directly.
* Customers. You will run our Customer Advisory Board, hold executive relationships at our largest accounts including the unhappy ones, and do the discovery and win and loss work behind the roadmap yourself. Sales will pull you into deals where the roadmap decides the outcome. This is a real share of your week.
* The cross-functional loop. Engineering is the closest partner, where you and their leadership run one roadmap queue and your PMs pair with their tech leads from shaping through release. Support, Implementation, Forward Deployed Engineering, CX, Marketing, and Finance each need something different from you, and all of them need to know what is coming before a customer does.
* BigTime Delivery. Not the day to day, but the calls on what we fix and when we stop, including when it needs engineering time the new platform was counting on.

**What We Are Looking For**

* 8+ years in product management for the Director level, 10+ for Senior Director, including at least three years managing PMs.
* B2B SaaS experience on a product with real operational or financial depth.
* You have built something new at a company that already had customers to protect. A replatform, a migration, or a net new product running alongside an existing one. Tell us what went wrong and what went well.

* You have developed PMs.

------------

* 8+ years in B2B product marketing, including leading a team of product marketers

* HR tech or recruiting technology background, or existing relationships with talent and HR leaders

Backed by a passionate team, our mission is to make pet care simple, accessible, and joyful for all. Because pets aren't just animals—they're family.

Yourgi grows two ways: pet parents completing bookings on our marketplace, and businesses running their operations on our software. This role owns the product strategy behind both and runs Product day to day. You’ll report to the Chief Product & Technology Officer (CPTO) and lead four product managers across five teams:
  
  
Bookings owns the booking flow and everything a pet parent does after booking.
  
  
Match owns search, ranking, and the experience before booking.
  
  
Pro owns the tools pros use to run their business.
  
  
Connect makes a national network of centers bookable online.
  
  
Centers runs online booking for Destination Pet locations.
  
  
Each team owns a customer journey end to end and pairs with an engineering lead and a designer.

jobs.title: Head of Product Marketing
jobs.desc:
**The role**
------------

We're in the midst of the most important buildout in U.S. history, with large growth across energy, transmission, commercial/industrial, housing, and conservation + carbon. Land is the bottleneck for all of these efforts. Aarden is a purpose-built solution to understand, invest in, and get deals done for land-dependent assets.

While only 16 months old, we are already working with the most important landowners and developers in the country, and it's time for the world to know about us. That's where you come in.

As Head of Product Marketing, your job is to show the market how Aarden thinks about land, in public, every week, and use that as a launching point to make Aarden the most influential and important voice in land markets. When a hyperscaler announces a campus, a county passes a moratorium, or a timber owner sells a million acres, you'll use Aarden to figure out what it means within the broader market context, what owners and developers should be doing in response, and what new opportunities it creates. Aarden is used to help clients make decisions like this every day, and your job is to elevate these capabilities to a much broader audience.

Over time, we want Aarden (and its leadership) to be who people turn to when they want to understand how America's land is changing, and we want that attention to turn into conversations with the landowners, developers, and investors who make the world move.

**About Aarden**
----------------

Aarden is the origination and investment partner for people building on and making decisions about American land, starting with the landowners and developers behind the energy & data center buildouts. For institutional timber and farmland owners, that means helping them see what their land could become and how to value it. For developers, it means finding willing owners with viable sites before sinking months of time and capital into a site that faces significant headwinds. For everyone, it means understanding the environmental and social impacts of these important decisions.

Under the hood, our platform combines parcel data, ownership resolution, zoning, community sentiment, and price signals with suitability models and defensible investment analysis.

We're a Seattle-based team, growing quickly and founded in 2025, with expansion plans into NYC in 2027. Four of the ten largest U.S. landowners are already clients, and our committed clients cover roughly 14 million acres of high value land. We have a wonderful cohort of investors as well. Our $4m pre-seed was announced last year but our subsequent fundraising efforts remain undisclosed; you would help us announce this.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* **Hunt for stories.** Read the news every day across data centers, energy, timber, farmland, and land policy, and comment on key events that change land markets (there are a lot of these!).
* **Use Aarden to find the answer.** Work with Aarden technology to figure out what each event means, lay out the options it creates for owners and developers, and back it up with historical and present-day patterns. Our data team will support you in this work.
* **Build Aarden's following on LinkedIn and X.** Publish several times a week across the company's and leadership's channels, and grow those audiences. You'll develop your own voice along the way, too.
* **Tell client stories.** Highlight our clients' efforts and help them grow their businesses with case studies that show how the smartest investors in the country partner with Aarden to drive results for their funds.
* **Turn attention into pipeline.** The stories we tell should help more organizations see the clear benefits of partnering with Aarden.
* **Speak to both sides of the market.** Write for timber and farmland owners who are weighing alternative uses, and for data center developers who are quite literally racing to secure sites. Help each learn about the benefits of working with the other.
* **Make Aarden

**About EnerVenue**

EnerVenue is a Silicon Valley-based energy infrastructure company commercializing metal-hydrogen battery technology originally developed by NASA for the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station. Founded in 2020 by Stanford Professor Yi Cui, EnerVenue adapts this proven aerospace chemistry for grid-scale terrestrial energy storage, delivering batteries with 30,000+ cycle lifetimes, inherent fire-safety, and a 30-year design life.

In 2026, EnerVenue closed a $300 million Series B extension and is well capitalized for growth. Funds are being deployed to build a high-volume manufacturing facility in Changzhou, China, targeting 250 MWh capacity by Q3 2026 and 1 GWh by 2027. EnerVenue has been named one of Time magazine's Top 10 US Green Technology Companies of 2025.

**The Role**

The Product Management Director reports directly to the Chief Product Officer and owns the full product lifecycle of EnerVenue's metal-hydrogen energy storage portfolio, from the Ni-H2 vessel and module, to racks, containerized and skid-mounted energy storage systems, and the accompanying BMS/EMS software layer. You are the single point of ownership connecting the market to the technology: translating utility, C&I and international customer needs into a prioritized roadmap, clear product requirements, defensible pricing, and products that R&D can design and the factory can build at scale.

This is a build-and-scale mission rather than a caretaking role. You will establish the product management function from the ground up: the roadmap process, the stage-gate NPI governance, the product cost and margin model, the competitive intelligence engine and the launch playbook. You will align product strategy with the company's gigawatt capacity roadmap, drive continuous reduction of levelized cost of storage (LCOS), and make the disciplined trade-off decisions across performance, cost, certification and time-to-market that determine whether each product wins in its target segment.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Product Strategy & Roadmap Ownership**

* Define and own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap for the full metal-hydrogen storage portfolio: cells and vessels, modules, racks, containerized/skid systems, and BMS/EMS software.
* Segment the market by application (utility-scale, C&I, microgrid, long-duration storage, harsh-environment and off-grid) and geography, and define the target product configuration, differentiation and value proposition for each segment.
* Build and maintain the business case for every product line: addressable market, volume forecast, price and cost trajectory, margin, investment requirement and payback.
* Align the product roadmap with the company's gigawatt capacity plan, R&D technology roadmap and go-to-market priorities; arbitrate scope, sequencing and resource allocation across competing initiatives.

**2. Market, Customer & Competitive Intelligence**

* Run a structured voice-of-customer program with utilities, IPPs, developers, EPCs, integrators and channel partners; convert field insight into prioritized requirements.
* Maintain continuous competitive intelligence across LFP and other lithium chemistries, flow batteries, sodium-ion and long-duration storage technologies; quantify EnerVenue's advantage in cycle life, safety, temperature tolerance and total lifetime cost.
* Track policy, incentive, tariff, grid-code and standards developments in target markets, and translate the implications into roadmap and positioning decisions.
* Own LCOS and total-cost-of-ownership models used in customer-facing value engineering and internal product decisions.

**3. Requirements Definition & NPI Governance**

* Author and own market requirement documents (MRD) and product requirement documents (PRD), translating customer and application needs into unambiguous, testable engineering specifications.
* Establish and chair the stage-gate NPI process from concept, design, prototype and pilot trial
