jobs.title: Technical Product Manager
jobs.desc:
**Facilities Management eXpress** is currently seeking a **Technical Product Manager** to join our team!

Do you build things instead of writing documents about them? Do repeated manual tasks make you want to open your laptop and fix them? If AI coding tools are just how you work, keep reading.

Much of FMX’s data starts in mechanical rooms, on rooftops, and in partner spreadsheets, and collecting it is slow and expensive. You’ll start by making our Facility Condition Assessments dramatically cheaper and faster. Then you’ll bring that approach to everywhere else data enters FMX.

You’ll be the product manager for these tools and usually the one building them, going from “huh, that’s painful” to a shipped fix in days. You’ll also spend more time on site than anyone in Product, so you’ll be our scout for the problems that never become support tickets.

**As the Technical Product Manager, you will:**

*First priority: make the FCA operation as efficient as possible*

* Own the cost and cycle time of an assessment. Baseline cost per building and square foot, technician hours, days on site, report turnaround, and rework rates, then set targets with Professional Services and report on them.
* Tackle the biggest time sinks first, across scoping, on-site capture, data cleanup, report production, and capital plan population.
* Build, ship, and support the FCA tools: the capture app and field workflow, operations tracking, the mapping and floor plan pipeline, and partner data intake.
* Get on site and do the work yourself, interviewing technicians and facilities staff and routing what you learn to the right product manager.

*Broader scope: data ingestion and the cost of operations*

* Cut the cost of bringing customer data into FMX during onboarding, from equipment lists and floor plans to formats nobody planned for.
* Build tooling that makes data intake repeatable instead of bespoke.
* Improve data completeness, not just speed. Thin data gathered quickly is worse than good data gathered efficiently.
* Use AI where it removes real work, like reading nameplate photos and floor plans, drafting condition narratives, and catching gaps before customers do.
* Automate internal work anywhere a small tool saves real time or money.
* When an internal tool earns a place in the FMX product, make the case and hand it off well, with documentation and data model implications.
* Keep the data defensible. Speed only counts if the work holds up.

*What success looks like in year one:*

* You know our cost and cycle time per assessment by heart, because you built the reporting.
* Technician hours or days per assessment are measurably down, thanks to what you shipped.
* The field team wouldn’t give up your tools, and Product makes decisions based on what you bring back.
* You’ve applied the same approach to at least one other ingestion problem, likely onboarding, and cut real cost.

  
**Requirements**

**Preferred Experience & Qualities:**

* + **A portfolio of shipped work.** This matters most. You’ve built and shipped real tools, and you can walk us through what you made, what broke, and how you fixed it.
  + **Daily AI-assisted building.** You use tools like Claude, Claude Code, or Cursor every day and have shipped working software with them.
  + **Enough coding skill to be dangerous.** You can read a stack trace, understand what an API is doing, work in git, deploy to something like Vercel, and catch the AI when it’s confidently wrong. No CS degree required.
  + **An outcome-driven mindset.** You’d rather own a number than a backlog, and watching cost or cycle time drop is what motivates you.
  + **Comfort in the field.** Mechanical rooms, roof hatches, hard hats, and long days walking buildings sound fun to you. You can travel up to 50% and have a valid driver’s license.
  + **Strong listening skills.** You can earn the trust of a maintenance tech and a facilities director in the same afternoon and get straight answers from both.

jobs.title: Product Manager – Roadmap Track (Sunshine Island)
jobs.desc:
As the Product Manager for the Roadmap Track, you will own the long-term features, core game loops, and retention systems that keep Sunshine Island, our flagship casual farming title, growing.

Our product team operates in two specialized execution tracks: Strategic Roadmap (deep features, long-term systems) and LiveOps (recurring events, monetization, D2C growth). You will lead the Roadmap Track in a close PM/PJM pair, partnering directly with a dedicated Project Manager (PJM) who manages day-to-day agile mechanics and operational scheduling. This structure frees you to focus on product direction, new mechanics, and the impact of what we build. You work with a complete feature team of dedicated engineers, designers, economy designers, artists, and data analysts, bringing new mechanics to a mature game.

This position is ideal for a data-driven Product Manager who thinks in roadmaps, stays close to the market to see what works, comes up with their own ideas for new mechanics, and wants to have a measurable impact on retention and long-term revenue.

#### **YOUR MISSION**

* Roadmap & Feature Ownership: Own the Roadmap Track backlog and quarterly plan. Keep existing features and systems healthy (progression, content updates, guilds, tournaments) while prioritizing and sequencing larger releases that move our KPIs.
* New Mechanics & Market Insight: Stay close to the market: play and analyze games in the genre, see what works, and come up with your own ideas for new mechanics that make the game better in its genre. Game designers own the detailed feature design, and you bring the ideas, the evidence, and the KPI goals.
* Retention & Early Game: Own first-session and early-game retention (FTUE, unlock pacing, onboarding) and the path from new player to veteran, working with analysts on cohorts and A/B tests.
* Progression & Content: Shape progression and content cadence with economy designers (content waves, level cap, progression speed), so players keep finding new things to do from the first session to veteran play.
* KPI Ownership & Testing: Own the roadmap KPIs: D7 and early retention, veteran DAU and ARPDAU of high-level players, and progression speed. Define success metrics up front and read A/B tests and cohorts together with the data analysts.
* Delivery & Collaboration: Partner with your track PJM on sprint scoping and release scheduling and act as the central product anchor for the feature team. Drive multi-phase features from goal to release, with clear scope and learnings per phase. You report to the Director of LiveOps and work day to day with the game's Product Owner.

#### **YOUR PROFILE**

* 4–6 years as a Product Manager or Game PM in mobile F2P gaming (casual, farming, simulation, or city-builder experience preferred).
* Proven Live Game Experience: Demonstrated experience running a live game and thinking in roadmaps: prioritizing, sequencing, and delivering large features, and weighing trade-offs between them.
* Market-Informed Mindset: Plays and analyzes games in the genre, has a strong pulse on what works, and turns it into ideas for new mechanics. Comfortable with retention and monetization metrics (D7, ARPDAU, LTV, churn).
* Player & Systems Understanding: Understanding of what keeps players engaged over time: progression, onboarding, long-term retention systems, and how economy and content pacing work together.
* Cross-Functional Communicator: Skilled at aligning and inspiring cross-functional teams (Art, Tech, Design, Analytics) through clear commercial reasoning without needing direct line management.
* Agile & Operationally Minded: Highly organized, calm under live operational pressure, and accustomed to working alongside PJMs in SCRUM/Kanban frameworks.
* Time Zone: Located within +/- 3 hours of CEST for real-time collaboration in our remote-first setup.
* AI-Savvy or Curious: Comfortable using AI tools in your daily work, or keen to learn. We use AI across production and expect you to try it.

Remote, United States
  

**About the role**

We are hiring a Product Manager to own the strategy, roadmap and commercial success of a line of hygienic sensors and instrumentation for the food, beverage and life sciences industries. You will turn customer and market insight into clear product requirements, work hand in hand with engineering to bring products to market, and equip sales to win. This role suits someone who is equally comfortable on a plant floor talking with a process engineer and in a business review defending a product's P&L.

**About us**

Anderson-Negele, a Ralliant company, designs and manufactures hygienic sensors for measuring temperature, level, pressure, flow and conductivity in sanitary processes. Our customers rely on our instruments to keep production safe, efficient and compliant. As part of Ralliant, we combine the focus of a specialist business with the resources of a global precision technology company.

**What you'll do**

* Own the product roadmap for your portfolio, balancing customer needs, technical feasibility and business return
* Build business cases for new products and enhancements, including market size, pricing, margin and launch forecasts
* Gather voice-of-customer input through site visits, interviews and work with sales and application engineers
* Write clear market and product requirements, and prioritize them with engineering through each development phase
* Lead product launches end to end: positioning, pricing, sales training, documentation and marketing materials
* Track portfolio performance (revenue, margin, quality, share) and act on what the numbers show
* Manage the product lifecycle, including end-of-life decisions and transition plans
Monitor competitors, industry standards (such as EHEDG and 3-A) and regulatory trends that affect your products  

**What you bring**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, a technical field or business
* 5+ years in product management, product marketing or application engineering for industrial or technical products
* A track record of taking products from concept to launch
* Strong financial sense: business cases, pricing and P&L ownership
* Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to align engineering, sales and leadership
Willingness to travel up to 25% to customers, trade shows and our sites  

**Nice to have**

* Experience with process instrumentation, sensors or automation in food, beverage, dairy or pharmaceutical markets
* Knowledge of hygienic design standards (EHEDG, 3-A, FDA) and digital connectivity technologies such as IO-Link
* Familiarity with stage-gate development
* MBA or equivalent business training

As one of the fastest growing SaaS start-up companies in the nation, we’re focused on finding the best talent and building the best team to continue accelerating our rapid growth to keep up with our demand.

Who You Are:

As an AlertMedia Product Manager you will have a primary role in setting the vision for our products while also playing an integral part in the day-to-day activities to make the vision a reality. Every day you’ll employ your ability to move smoothly between cross-functional teams, inspiring, learning and leading. Time with customers will be one of your best sources of improvements and new feature ideas. Best of all, you’ll be part of AlertMedia’s amazing culture and an important contributor to our rapid growth.

You are passionate about your products, and maybe even a little obsessive. You see both the forest AND the trees. You are energetic, empathic and earnest. Collaborating with people across different functions comes naturally to you. You are known for your willingness to share information and having no ego. You refuse to give up when the path isn’t clear.

When a critical event unfolds, the hard part is rarely knowing that something happened — it is understanding the impact and coordinating the many steps, people, and systems that have to move in the right order, quickly, and often all at once. * Customer-focused approach to gathering requirements and delivering business value.

------------------

Bitsight's engineering organization is changing fast. AI tools now write and review a growing share of our code, and the path from ticket to shipped change is shifting with them. We need a Technical Product Manager to help prioritize and coordinate execution on improvements to our process.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.desc:
**Company**
-----------

Pramaana Labs is a frontier AI lab building the verification layer for AI. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Palo Alto, we turn complex human knowledge, including tax codes, legal rules, clinical guidelines and security protocols, into a formal representation, so every AI answer can be traced, challenged, and proved. Pramaana's architecture pairs foundation models trained to formalize and reason with a symbolic world model encoded in Lean 4. Pramaana was founded by a team out of Google, DeepMind, and Glean, combining frontier AI researchers and formal methods experts.

**The Role**
------------

We’re looking for a hands-on Product Manager to turn Pramaana’s formalization and verification capabilities into products people use and trust. You’ll own a product area from discovering the problem through launch and adoption, working closely with engineering, research, design, domain experts, and our commercial team.

Our planned product areas include the self-serve workbench and developer experience, Harbor for tax, and government products. Each PM will have a defined product area; this shared draft can be tailored to the relevant audience and workflow. You’ll help establish direction, make practical trade-offs, and stay close to users as the product evolves.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Discover valuable problems. Talk to users, observe workflows, and identify where formalization and verification can deliver a measurable improvement.
* Own product direction and priorities. Define the target user, use cases, roadmap, and success measures for your product area. Make clear choices about what to build next and why.
* Translate technical capabilities into usable workflows. Define requirements, user journeys, and acceptance criteria with engineering, research, design, and domain experts.
* Make verification understandable. Help users inspect sources, assumptions, supporting evidence, unresolved questions, and changes without overstating what the system has established.
* Drive delivery and iteration. Scope experiments and releases, resolve dependencies, test with users, and follow through on quality and adoption after launch.
* Measure outcomes. Track activation, repeat usage, task completion, time to value, and product quality; use evidence to guide decisions.
* Partner with the commercial team. Support demos and customer discovery, bring market feedback into the roadmap, and distinguish reusable product needs from customer-specific implementation requests.

**You Will Thrive in This Role If You Have**
--------------------------------------------

* Experience taking a technical product from an ambiguous problem to shipped software and sustained usage, with clear examples of your decisions and their outcomes.
* Strong customer discovery and product judgment. You can identify the underlying need, test assumptions, and prioritize with limited time and resources.
* Technical fluency. You can discuss APIs, data flows, model behavior, and system constraints with engineers and researchers, then translate them into clear product choices.
* Ability to lead across functions through clear reasoning, practical scoping, and follow-through.
* Comfort with information-rich workflows where correctness, evidence, and user trust matter.

**Especially Strong Candidates May Also Have**
----------------------------------------------

* Experience with developer tools, self-serve software, enterprise AI, or products used in regulated workflows.
* Relevant tax or government workflow experience for the corresponding vertical role.
* Experience as an early PM, establishing product practices and helping a technical team find repeatable adoption.

**GTM Product Manager**
-----------------------

* **Location:** Preferred: MA, CT, OH, or NY (hybrid); other US locations also considered
* **Department:** Applied Innovation
* **Reports To:** SVP, Applied Innovation

### **About OpinionRoute**

At OpinionRoute, we are redefining how Market Research Agencies run their operations. From programming to sample to data quality and data visualization, we are building the technology not usually accessible to the MRA.  
  
The Navigator (our research operating system) runs the whole project process. Our market-leading Data Quality & Fraud Prevention suite (CleanID, ResponseID, QC Flow) mitigates today’s toughest quality threats. Our enhanced survey Programming & Hosting services are how we make more dynamic surveys for forward-thinking researchers.

We are built for researchers, not investors. Our mission is to take the chaos out of market research operations through modern automation, AI-assisted quality control, and frictionless workflows.

### **The Role**

This role sits between the teams that build our technology and the teams that sell, deliver, and use it. You will report directly to our SVP of Applied Innovation.

**Product Manager**

We're building a world-class, AI-driven operating system for local government, and we want product managers who can help shape it from day one.

**The role**

You'll own a product area end to end, with real customers, real usage and real influence on where the platform goes. Not a backlog someone else wrote, and not a feature inside a feature.

You'll work across our finance and operations suite, in areas like document management, accounts payable, reporting and analytics, and payroll and HR. Where you focus will be matched to your background and where the business needs it most.

If you're a PM today on an HR, payroll, AP or finance product, at a govtech or software vendor large or small, and you're ready for more ownership, faster decisions and AI at the center of the product, this is that job.

**What you'll do**

* **Own the roadmap for your area.** Decide what we build, what we don't, and why, then back it up with customer evidence and data.
* **Build AI into the core workflow.** Find the manual, repetitive work in your domain (keying invoices, reconciling payroll, building month-end reports) and design AI and agentic features that remove it.
* **Work shoulder to shoulder with engineering.** Write clear specs, user stories and acceptance criteria, make trade-offs in real time, and ship in short cycles on an API-first platform.
* **Partner with sales, implementation and support.** Join deals, demo what's coming, turn field feedback into product, and make sure every launch lands with the teams who sell and support it.
* **Spend real time with customers.** Clerks, finance directors, payroll admins and treasurers. Watch the work and bring back what you learn.
* **Measure what matters.** Set outcomes for adoption, time saved, support volume and revenue, and report on them.
* **Help modernize the platform.** Shape how capabilities move onto our new platform without disrupting anyone's month-end close.

**Your first 90 days:** learn the domain and the customers, ship your first meaningful improvement, and publish a 12-month roadmap for your area.

**What you bring**

**Must have**

* 3-4 years as a Product Manager or Product Owner on B2B SaaS.
* In your current role, you manage an HR, payroll, AP, finance, document management or reporting product, at a govtech, public-sector ERP or finance/HR software company. This needs to be your job today, not a past role.
* Shipped at least one software product in that space, end to end, that customers use today, and can walk us through what you built and the results.
* You use AI tools every day in your own work (prototyping, research, writing specs, analyzing data) and have opinions on where AI belongs in a product and where it doesn't.
* Comfortable going deep with engineers on APIs, data models and trade-offs, then explaining the same thing plainly to a customer or a salesperson.
* A track record of shipping. You can point to things you launched and what changed because of them.
* High drive and low ego. You want ownership, you move fast, and you'd rather fix the problem than describe it.

**Nice to have**

* Public-sector, fund accounting, municipal finance or utility billing experience.
* Experience on an ERP or HCM suite, especially a cloud migration or legacy-to-new-platform rebuild.
* Shipped an AI or LLM-powered feature to production (document extraction, copilots, agents, natural-language reporting).
* Comfort with SQL or a BI tool so you can answer your own questions.

**Why join us**

* **Ownership from day one.** Here you own an area, not a screen, and work directly with product and technology leadership.
* **AI is the strategy, not a side project.** We're building the platform AI-first, so your ideas ship instead of waiting on a corporate AI program.
* **Real customers, real scale.** 2,000+ local governments already run on our products. What you build gets used the week it ships.

**Advanced Specialist Product Manager – Test Security Platforms**

**Summary**

Pearson Professional Assessments delivers the exam and testing ecosystem that professional bodies, regulators, certification programmes and schools depend on to make high-stakes decisions about people. Security is not a feature of that service. It is the service.

The role is accountable for five security domains: Identity, Behavior, Location, Platform and Environment - and for the platforms and shared services that deliver them, across market-facing and internal applications alike. It includes the security capability roadmap for the online-proctored channel.

The role exists because our security capability today is strong but application-shaped. Controls have grown up inside individual products, driven largely by what individual clients asked for, and the same problem has been solved more than once in more than one place. We are moving to a model where security is a deliberately designed shared platform, built from a standing read of the threat landscape and the market rather than from inbound requirements.

**Key responsibilities**

***Domain and platform product ownership***

* Own a persistent, outcome-based roadmap for each of the five domains — refreshed continuously against evidence, not reset annually by the project cycle.
* Design security as a shared platform. Define the capabilities, service contracts and integration patterns that channel and application teams consume, so a control is built once and applied everywhere it is needed.
* Maintain a live capability gap analysis by domain. Be able to answer, at any time, which assurance is weakest and what it would take to close it.

***Market intelligence and outside-in discovery***

* Build and maintain a standing view of the exam security threat landscape — AI-assisted cheating, proxy testing, content harvesting, organised fraud, emerging spoofing techniques — and use it as the primary input to the roadmap.
* Track competitor and adjacent-industry capability deliberately and continuously. Know where we lead, match or lag, by domain, and say so plainly.
* Run continuous discovery with candidates, proctors, test centre staff, client programme owners, and our own forensics and operations teams. Discovery is a habit, not a phase at the start of a project.
* Convert single-client requests into capabilities that serve the whole book of business. Decline bespoke security work with a reasoned, evidenced alternative rather than a refusal.

***Evidence, measurement and model performance***

* Instrument every control. Own the metrics that show whether a capability is actually working: detection rate, precision and recall, false-positive burden, appeal and overturn rates, candidate and proctor impact.
* Partner with data science and analytics on AI and ML-based detection. Set the performance bar, own the precision/recall position, and understand what both error directions cost a real candidate.
* **Ensure the evidence a control produces** **is** **defensible** — capable of standing up to candidate appeal, client scrutiny, regulator questions and legal challenge. A detection we cannot evidence is not a detection.
* Close the loop: forensics findings, incident reviews and result holds from live delivery feed straight back into the roadmap.

***Delivery partnership***

* Work as one team with Engineering Delivery, Architecture and Security Operations — from discovery through production and into operational life.
* Write clearly. Crisp problem statements, decision records and product narratives that a senior engineer, a client and an executive can each read and act on.
* Sequence around outcomes and dependencies, and be accountable for what reaches production — not for the plan.

***Advancing how we work***

* Replace project-shaped intake with durable product ownership in your area, and show the rest of the portfolio what good looks like.
* Coach and partner with programme and project management colleagu

Radar helps businesses prevent fraud and abuse without getting in the way of legitimate customers. We combine machine learning powered by Stripe’s global network with intuitive dashboard experiences and developer APIs, to give our users comprehensive controls and insights to protect their business against threats ranging from payment fraud and card testing to bot and free trial abuse.

Fraud doesn’t stand still, and it isn’t limited to checkout. As businesses launch new products and business models, attackers find new ways to exploit them. We obsess about understanding those attacks, identifying defenses that work, and making sophisticated fraud prevention simple for the businesses that depend on us to help them protect and grow their revenue with confidence.

What you’ll do

As a product manager on the Radar team, you’ll work directly with customers to understand the novel fraud and abuse attacks they face, identify the most important problems to solve, and turn those insights into product strategy and a roadmap.

You’ll work at the intersection of customers, engineering, data science, design, and commercial teams to shape what we build and bring it to market. Your work will span the fraud and abuse detection and control capabilities at the heart of Radar and the user and developer experiences that put those capabilities into our customers’ hands.

This role requires both urgency and taste. You’ll move quickly as threats evolve, without compromising on reliability, craft, or the details that make complex products feel beautifully simple.

  • Develop a deep understanding of the fraud and abuse landscape.
  • Investigate emerging attacks with customers, assess their financial and operational impact, and distinguish isolated incidents from opportunities to build broadly useful defenses.

  • Partner with engineering, data science, and design to explore signals, shape solutions, and rapidly turn effective defenses into scalable, reliable products.
  • Set the pace for the team by scoping the product thoughtfully, prioritizing ruthlessly, and executing with high rigor.
  • Work with sales, marketing, and customer-facing teams to validate demand, coordinate launches, and help customers adopt and maximize the value they get from new capabilities.
  • Own product performance, user experience, and business metrics to guide iteration and communicate progress.

Who you are

Minimum requirements

  • 8+ years of Product Management experience

  • Scrappy and resourceful, with experience taking products from zero to one. You find ways to test ideas quickly, learn from real users, and turn early solutions into products that scale.

This position is fully funded and ready for impact.

Declarative workflow systems and operational decision-support tools

Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 14 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 5 years as a Product Owner or in a comparable role

jobs.desc:
**JLL empowers you to shape a brighter way**.

Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology for our clients. We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people and empowering them to thrive, grow meaningful careers and to find a place where they belong. Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades or technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, join our team as we help shape a brighter way forward.

**ServiceNow Product Manager** 
 
**Purpose of the Role**
=========================================================

JLL's Enterprise Service Management (ESM) team is hiring a ServiceNow Product Manager to own ServiceNow as a strategic enterprise platform. This role is accountable end-to-end for the platform's product strategy.

The Product Manager is expected to help transform ESM into a value-providing function for JLL — treating ServiceNow as a product with a strategy and a roadmap rather than infrastructure to be kept running and ensuring platform investment is justified by measurable business outcomes rather than ticket volume or license spend alone.

Three key qualifications are necessary to be successful in this role: (1) strong platform/product management skill — the ability to own a strategic enterprise SaaS platform's roadmap, backlog, and license/consumption economics across multiple, often competing stakeholder groups; (2) ITSM/ITIL expertise at large-enterprise scale, paired with a proven, hands-on record of using AI and agentic AI to modernize a ServiceNow or ITSM practice; and (3) critical thinking and analytical judgment — the ability to apply industry frameworks, staffing models, and vendor claims appropriately to JLL's business rather than adopting them by rote.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Platform Product Strategy & Roadmap Ownership**

* Own end-to-end product strategy and the multi-year roadmap for JLL's ServiceNow platform, acting as the single Product Manager accountable for what gets built, extended, or retired on the platform and why.
* Translate ESM's operating model and business demand into a prioritized platform roadmap, arbitrating competing requests.
* Define and maintain the platform's product backlog, working with the Director, ITSM Platform & Automation Lead to translate roadmap priorities into engineering delivery.
* Build the business case and secure ESM leadership buy-in for major platform investments, module additions, and multi-year initiatives.

**License, Consumption & Value Management**

* Own ServiceNow license and module portfolio management — tracking consumption, utilization, and entitlement against actual usage to prevent both under-licensing risk and shelfware spend.
* Own the ROI/value case for the platform, defining and reporting the business-outcome metrics (adoption, self-service deflection, automation coverage, cost avoidance) that justify continued and future investment.

**Cross-Tower Governance & Release Management**

* Partner with the CMDB Product Owner, Change Enablement Process Owner, and other ESM process owners so platform roadmap decisions stay aligned with data governance and change/release policy.
* Own platform governance standards — configuration, customization, and technical-debt discipline — in partnership with engineering, so the platform does not fragment as adoption grows across towers.
* Apply critical thinking to distinguish JLL's genuine platform needs from vendor sales narratives, and defend prioritization trade-offs to senior stakeholders when demand exceeds capacity

**AI & Agentic Platform Enablement**

* Own the platform-level roadmap for AI and agentic capability — ServiceNow's native AI Agent Studio, AI Agent Orchestrator, and Now Assist — partnering with the ITSM Engineering Manager and Intelligent Automation Lead on what gets built and adopted, and in what sequence.
* Bring critical, ev

jobs.desc:
**Product Owner, NDA Solutions**
================================

Information Technology · Atlanta, GA (Hybrid) · Full-time, Exempt

National Distribution Alliance (NDA) runs several platforms supporting the group purchasing organization, its operators, and its supplier programs, and this role owns them. The near-term job is integration: bringing systems that overlap toward one coherent experience instead of several disconnected ones.

You’ll set the roadmap, decide what gets built next, hold the technology partners to it, and stand behind the data and reporting that NDA and its Suppliers make decisions on.

The role is designed to work as one of a pair, alongside a counterpart Product Owner covering the National Distribution Alliance (NDA). You’ll each own your own business unit, back each other up, and work to one shared set of standards so a capability needed by both gets built once. Where that counterpart role isn’t in place yet, you’ll carry an agreed level of support for the other business unit in the meantime, scoped with IT and business unit leadership rather than left to absorb informally.

**About UniPro**
----------------

We’re a cooperative of independent foodservice distributors. Our Members compete against companies many times their size, and they win by staying closer to their customers and moving faster. UniPro gives them the scale, buying power, supplier relationships, and increasingly the data and technology that would otherwise be out of reach.

These platforms are how Members, distributors, and operators actually do business with us. Keeping them accurate and dependable is what this role is for.

**What you’ll do**
------------------

**Own the platforms and the roadmap**

* Act as the primary business owner for NDA’s platforms, making sure each one supports its reporting, operational, and data quality objectives.
* Keep a prioritized enhancement roadmap, informed by talking to operators, distributors, Members, Suppliers, and internal users rather than only by whatever lands in the request queue, and be clear about the trade-offs.
* Push the portfolio toward fewer and better systems: consolidate overlapping systems into one coherent experience, and drive newly implemented platforms from launch to dependable.
* Run the technology partner relationships as the main point of contact for enhancement requests, issues, testing, implementation status, and platform updates. Lead evaluations, renewals, and statements of work, and hold partners to the scope, timelines, and service levels agreed.
* Turn business needs into clear requirements and acceptance criteria, coordinate testing and rollout, and accept or reject releases against the criteria agreed up front.
* Lead recurring stakeholder meetings, including agendas, action item tracking, and communicating decisions.
* Decide what success looks like for each significant release and report afterward on whether you got there. If something ships and nobody uses it, that’s yours to fix.

**Keep the data right**

* Run the daily, weekly, and monthly validations that keep platform data complete, timely, accurate, and ready to report on, along with the mapping and reconciliation behind reliable reporting.
* Chase missing, late, incomplete, or inaccurate submissions, find the root cause, and get it corrected with distributors and other data providers.
* Audit incoming files and data sources, troubleshoot file errors, and coordinate corrections and resubmissions. Escalate anything that could affect reporting accuracy, operational visibility, supplier programs, or business decisions.
* Maintain master data integrity across product, distributor, operator, and Member attributes, and own the data standards, documentation, governance procedures, and quality thresholds.
* Work with our data team so definitions, metrics, and thresholds stay consistent with UniPro’s wider reporting.
* Validate new reports, dashboards, and calculations before release, spot check live reporting aga

Role Overview

The Product Manager / Product Owner – AI is responsible for end-to-end ownership of AI initiatives for a specific Line of Business or claims domain. This role partners directly with business stakeholders to define AI-enabled improvements to claims operations, cost control, and client service performance, and translates those objectives into structured, sprint-ready execution plans.

This role combines strategic initiative shaping with hands-on backlog ownership and daily collaboration with AI engineers and data scientists. It ensures that AI development is grounded in real operational pain points and that delivered solutions are practical, compliant, and measurable in impact.

Key Responsibilities

The Product Manager/Owner works directly with claims leadership, operational managers, and Business Transformation Leads to understand workflow bottlenecks, leakage drivers, customer friction points, regulatory risks, and client performance commitments. They translate these insights into clearly defined AI use cases with measurable operational objectives such as reduced claim cycle time, improved reserving accuracy, enhanced fraud detection rates, or improved document processing speed.

They decompose initiatives into epics and features that reflect real-world operational workflows, ensuring requirements account for system integrations, adjuster behavior, client reporting requirements, and compliance obligations. They collaborate with AI engineers and data scientists to validate feasibility, data availability, model explainability considerations, and downstream operational impact.

They own and continuously refine the product backlog, ensuring it remains prioritized according to business value and aligned with enterprise AI portfolio constraints. They prepare stories with detailed acceptance criteria that reflect actual claims scenarios and operational realities, not abstract technical requirements.

During sprint execution, they remain closely engaged with the delivery team, clarifying nuances of claims processes, regulatory rules, and client-specific variations. They validate that developed models, automation features, or decision-support tools function appropriately within the claims workflow and align with user expectations.

They communicate progress, risks, and trade-offs to LOB stakeholders transparently, ensuring expectations are managed around sequencing and delivery timelines. Following deployment, they monitor adoption, operational metrics, and user feedback, adjusting backlog priorities based on real-world performance and measurable impact.

This role requires balancing operational urgency with disciplined backlog governance, particularly in environments where client escalations or regulatory deadlines may introduce pressure for rapid change.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.desc:
**Why we exist**
----------------

Most people with treatment-resistant depression, PTSD, or OCD spend years cycling through medications before anyone mentions there are other options. Treatments like accelerated TMS, SAINT, Spravato, and IV ketamine can work when nothing else has. They're also hard to find, hard to get covered, and hard to deliver well. That gap is why Radial exists.

We support the country's largest network of brain medicine clinics: 27 clinics and more than 100 clinicians across seven states, caring for patients with some of the most serious mental health conditions there are. RadialOS, our AI-native operating system, matches patients to the right treatment, coordinates their care, and takes administrative work off clinicians' plates. We're backed by General Catalyst, and in 2026 we acquired the MSO behind Mindful Health Solutions, one of the pioneers of interventional psychiatry.

Every role here supports our mission of getting patients access to the care they need as quickly as possible.

**The role**
------------

Our patients feel every broken handoff. A referral comes in, gets entered in one system, checked against insurance in another, and scheduled in a third. Somewhere in between, someone with severe depression waits. This PM's job is to find those places and remove them.

You'll sit closer to the work than anyone else on the product team. That could mean working the front desk during the Monday-morning call rush, shadowing a technician through a day of accelerated TMS sessions, or sitting beside a biller as they chase a Spravato prior authorization across three payer portals. Then you'll go back and fix what you saw.

The scope is wide and the autonomy is real. The distance between seeing a problem at a front desk and shipping the fix is short, and we want to keep it that way.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Map how work actually happens across our clinics and operations teams, including the workarounds nobody wrote down.
* Find where time, revenue, and patients fall out of the process, and size each problem so we know which to fix first.
* Decide what to build, buy, or automate, then ship it with engineering, design, and clinical leaders.
* Prototype with AI yourself so ideas get tested in days, not quarters.
* Write PRFAQs and short specs that make the decision obvious.
* Roll changes out across 27 clinics, train the people who'll use them, and measure whether they worked.
* Own outcomes like time to first appointment, prior authorization turnaround, clinician admin time, and patient experience.

**Backgrounds we think could thrive here**
------------------------------------------

* Former health-tech founders who want high ownership and direct contact with users
* Engineers moving into product who still like building the first prototype themselves
* Health-tech PMs who want to be in the room where their product gets used
* Clinic or practice operators who taught themselves to build with AI and want to do it full time
* Builders who care deeply about data models and it impacts front-end workflows

This list isn't a checklist. If you see yourself in one of these, we'd like to talk. If you don't but the role still sounds like you, we'd like to talk too.

**You may be a great fit if you**
---------------------------------

* Have watched someone use something you built and changed the plan because of what you saw.
* Build a rough version the same afternoon when the tool you need doesn't exist.
* Can explain the same tradeoff to a clinician, an engineer, and an executive, and each one trusts you.
* Narrow ambiguity instead of waiting for someone to resolve it for you.
* Earn trust fast with frontline teams, because you show up, listen, and come back with something that helps.
* Reach for AI first. You build your own tools and agents and have opinions about where AI helps and where it doesn't.

We're open on seniority. Strong candidates may have three years of product experience or ten, and

jobs.desc:
**About Agile Defense**

At Agile Defense we know that action defines the outcome and new challenges require new solutions. That’s why we always look to the future and embrace change with an unmovable spirit and the courage to build for what comes next.

Our vision is to bring adaptive innovation to support our nation's most important missions through the seamless integration of advanced technologies, elite minds, and unparalleled agility—leveraging a foundation of speed, flexibility, and ingenuity to strengthen and protect our nation’s vital interests.

**Requisition #:** 1959

**Job Title:** Product Manager/Fires SME

**Location:** Honolulu, HI | National Capital Region | On-site

**Clearance Level:** TS/SCI eligibility required

**Required Certification(s):** None

### **Summary**

A commander looking at a recommended target and effect pairing asks two questions: why this, and why now? Target Effect Pairing (TEP) is a capability for USPACOM Joint Fires, built on the Maven Smart System, that answers both with AI recommendations a targeting staff can trace, explain, and audit. It speeds up capabilities analysis and the commander's decision and force assignment, while every inherently governmental decision stays with a human. Engineers can build the software. They can't tell on their own whether it reflects how joint targeting is really done.

That judgment is yours. You bring operational targeting experience and the working habits of a product manager, and you turn joint targeting doctrine, JFE and JTCB workflows, and target development standards into requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria. You work with a Senior UX Designer, software engineers and architects, and a Technical Program Manager who owns backlog priority and government acceptance. You own whether what gets built is operationally right.

Requirements are still forming, and much of the team has never worked in targeting. The recommendations this capability produces will also be independently assessed for quality, so output that merely looks reasonable won't hold up.

**What Success Looks Like**

**Objective 1: In the first 90 days, give the team an accurate picture of how USPACOM targeting runs today**

* Government targeteers review your map of the current workflow, from target development through nomination, approval, and assessment, and confirm it is accurate.
* Engineers and designers can say where each JFE or JTCB decision happens, and who holds the authority for it, without coming to you first.
* Where the command's practice departs from doctrine, the gap is written down along with which one the product follows and why.

**Objective 2: Turn targeting doctrine and decision authority into requirements the team can build and test**

* Engineers build from your user stories and acceptance criteria without a rework cycle over operational intent.
* Every inherently governmental decision point appears in the requirements, with the human approval it needs spelled out.
* Feature requests reach the backlog framed as the operational problem behind them, not only as the feature someone asked for.
* The Technical Program Manager gets priority recommendations grounded in operational value, with the reasoning visible.

**Objective 3: By month six, prove that recommendations hold up before a commander sees them**

* Representative scenarios and acceptance criteria test whether a pairing recommendation is complete, relevant, and defensible.
* Each recommendation answers why this and why now, with its assumptions and limits stated plainly enough for a targeteer to challenge.
* Operational problems show up in your scenarios first, rather than in government evaluation.

**Objective 4: By the end of year one, make operator feedback what steers the product**

* Demonstrations with targeteers, JFE and JTCB staff, and J32 operators produce feedback that changes what gets built next.
* Each capability has measures of success agreed before it is built, and you report agai

Marlabs, a global AI and Digital Solutions Consulting firm, delivers intelligent solutions across AI, data, analytics, and product engineering. Since 2000, we have partnered with some of the largest healthcare, life sciences, financial services, and government organizations worldwide. As we continue to expand our global footprint, we have an exciting opportunity for a highly skilled Technical Product Owner (Strategy & Execution) to join our innovative and dynamic team.

**Technical Product Owner (Strategy & Execution) | About You**

As a Technical Product Owner (Strategy & Execution), you will help shape and execute technology strategy across enterprise digital initiatives, serving as the bridge between business leadership and technical delivery teams. You will partner with senior stakeholders, architects, engineers, and Agile teams to translate strategic objectives into actionable roadmaps, prioritized backlogs, and measurable outcomes. The ideal candidate combines strategic thinking with strong execution capabilities and can comfortably navigate cloud, data, analytics, AI, and platform initiatives while balancing long-term vision with day-to-day delivery priorities.

**Technical Product Owner (Strategy & Execution) | Day-to-Day**

* Partner with business and technology leaders to define strategic priorities, technology roadmaps, investment opportunities, and measurable business outcomes.

jobs.desc:
**Position Overview**

ScanSource is seeking a strategic, value driven, execution-focused Product Owner to lead and own the vision, roadmap, and delivery of scalable software platforms and solutions. This role is accountable for maximizing value across the full product lifecycle by translating business strategy, partner needs, customer experience goals, and operational requirements into a well-defined, prioritized product backlog. The Product Owner will serve as the primary decision-maker for product scope, priority, and aligns closely with technical teams ensuring products are built for scale, reuse, adoption, and measurable business impact across a multi-partner ecosystem.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

* While serving as the voice of the customer, own the vision, strategy, roadmap, and backlog for software platforms and solutions ensuring alignment to business objectives, partner growth goals, and customer experience priorities.
* Facilitate intake, prioritization, governance, and cross-functional decision-making to align stakeholders and maintain delivery momentum.
* Lead product discovery with stakeholders, users, and cross-functional teams to identify opportunities, validate needs, and define scalable platform capabilities.
* Define high-quality business requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and success measures that enable efficient execution and strong delivery outcomes.
* Drive the design and evolution of reusable platform capabilities while balancing standardization with configurable partner-specific needs.
* Partner closely with technical development, architecture, QA, operations, and support teams to clarify requirements, resolve issues, and deliver intuitive, scalable, and supportable solutions.
* Define, track, and communicate product KPIs, adoption metrics, and business value measures to guide prioritization and continuous improvement.
* Coordinate dependencies, risks, and release readiness across teams, systems, vendors, and partner stakeholders.
* Support rollout, change management, documentation and ongoing optimization to drive successful adoption and long-term product value realization.

  

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
* 5+ years of experience in product ownership, product management, business systems, or platform delivery roles, with demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional initiatives.
* Proven experience owning and prioritizing product backlogs, writing high-quality business requirements and user stories, and defining acceptance criteria that drive strong delivery outcomes.
* Experience with platform-based products, B2B commerce, partner ecosystems, channel operations, or enterprise application software solutions supporting multiple user groups and business models.
* Strong understanding of Agile product delivery, backlog management, release planning, and stakeholder governance.
* Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into executable roadmaps and detailed requirements while maintaining focus on customer value and measurable results.
* Excellent communication, facilitation, and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across business and technology teams.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including experience using data and metrics to drive prioritization and continuous improvement.

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

jobs.title: Product Manager, Lumina Data Platform
jobs.desc:
Overview

We are building a cloud-native data platform that ingests, governs, and serves data to product and analytics teams across the company. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own two tightly connected sides of that platform: the sourcing of data into the platform, and the experience of the internal teams who consume it. You will decide which data sources we onboard and how, define the contracts and standards that keep that data trustworthy, and treat the platform's internal consumers — product engineering, analytics, data science, Agentic AI, and operations teams — as your primary customers.

This is a high-leverage role. The quality, coverage, and usability of the platform directly shapes what dozens of downstream teams can ship. You will translate ambiguous, cross-functional needs into a clear roadmap, and you will be measured on adoption, data reliability, and the speed at which internal teams can build on what you provide.

Responsibilities

What You'll Own

  • Data sourcing strategy — prioritize and manage the pipeline of internal and third-party data sources to onboard; weigh coverage, cost, licensing, quality, and effort to decide what gets ingested and in what order.
  • Source onboarding — define the intake process for new sources, from evaluation and vendor/provider assessment through ingestion, validation, and go-live; partner with data engineering on connectors, schemas, and SLAs.
  • Data contracts & standards — establish the schema, freshness, quality, and metadata standards that every source must meet, and the governance for changing them without breaking consumers.
  • Consumer management — own the relationship with the internal teams that consume the platform; run intake for their requests, maintain a clear prioritization framework, and keep a feedback loop that turns their needs into roadmap.
  • Adoption & reliability — define and track the metrics that matter — source coverage, data freshness and quality, consumer adoption, and time-to-onboard a new consumer — and act on them.
  • Roadmap & stakeholders — maintain the platform roadmap, communicate trade-offs and timelines, and align sourcing investments with the priorities of the teams you serve.
  • AI-forward delivery — use AI tools as a default part of how the work gets done — accelerating source evaluation, requirements, documentation, and consumer support — and champion AI-assisted workflows across the platform and its consumer teams.

Qualifications

What You'll Do Day to Day

  • Interview and shadow internal consumer teams to understand how they use data and where the platform slows them down.

  • Write clear requirements and data contracts, and partner with engineering to size and sequence the work.

  • Evaluate new data sources — internal systems and external providers — and make the call on what to onboard.

  • Triage and prioritize the consumer request queue against a transparent framework.

  • Report on platform health and adoption to leadership and to the teams who depend on you.

  • Reach for AI to move faster — drafting specs and docs, summarizing consumer feedback, prototyping, and profiling new data sources — and share what works with the team.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years in product management, with meaningful time on data, platform, infrastructure, or API products serving internal or technical users.

  • Data platform fluency — comfortable reasoning about data pipelines, warehouses/lakes, schemas, data quality, and governance; you can hold a credible technical conversation with data engineers.

  • Cloud-native context — familiarity with modern cloud data stacks (e.g., object storage, managed warehouses, streaming/ELT, orchestration) and the trade-offs they carry.

jobs.desc:
**POSITION SUMMARY**

Owns strategy, discovery, and roadmap prioritization for an assigned product or product area, translating customer and market insight into a validated, prioritized set of initiatives. Operates within UKI’s AI-driven development lifecycle (ADLC): uses AI tooling to validate problems and solutions before engineering time is committed, building working prototypes where that is the fastest way to reduce uncertainty, and writes requirements that engineers and AI agents can execute against. Partners with UX Design and Engineering to drive features from concept through launch, and partners directly with Engineering on delivery.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Leads AI-accelerated discovery to validate problems and solutions before Engineering time is committed, partnering with UX Design on research, validation, and design review. When a working prototype is the fastest way to validate a problem, solution, or workflow, builds one with AI-assisted tools, tests it with customers and internal stakeholders, and carries the evidence into prioritization and requirements. Works alongside Engineering in the ADLC harness, from planning and selecting specialists and agents through the build, review, and fix loop, capturing learnings from each cycle and staying current on AI tooling. Writes unambiguous, testable requirements and acceptance criteria that engineers, designers, and AI agents can execute against, paired with a validated prototype or reference where one exists, and partners with Engineering to turn roadmap priorities into a delivery plan. Tracks and reports product-level success metrics after launch, and communicates roadmap status, tradeoffs, and risks to product leadership and stakeholders.

 **Requirements**

Required

* 3–5+ years of product management experience in B2B SaaS
* Experience owning discovery and roadmap decisions for a defined product area
* Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable saying no and explaining why
* Working familiarity with agile delivery models
* Hands-on fluency with AI-assisted prototyping and development tools (for example Claude, Cursor, Lovable, v0, or similar); able to produce a working prototype, not only a specification
* Experience working in an AI-assisted or AI-driven development lifecycle, or a demonstrated record of adopting new tooling and ways of working quickly

Preferred

* Experience with cybersecurity training, cyber ranges, workforce readiness, or learning platforms (LMS/LXP)
* Experience building for or selling to DoD, federal, or SLED customers, including familiarity with procurement, security, and compliance constraints
* Familiarity with cyber workforce competency frameworks (NICE Framework, DCWF, DoD 8140) and assessment-driven readiness models
* Prior Experience partnering with and directing a delivery team
* A portfolio of prototypes or shipped features you built or materially shaped with AI tooling

 **Benefits**

* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage.
* Short and long-term disability coverage for added security.
* Basic life insurance provided by the company.
* Optional supplementary life insurance policy available for additional coverage.
* UKI covers 100% of individual premiums for medical, dental, vision, disability, and basic life insurance.
* A 401k plan with a basic safe harbor matching (up to 4% match with a 5% contribution).
* Enjoy 15 days of PTO annually for vacation or sick leave.
* Benefit from 12 company holidays, aligning with 11 federal holidays, plus Christmas Eve.

The Product Manager is responsible for the strategy, roadmap, and complete life cycle of assigned product lines, from opportunity identification and concept development through launch, sustainment, and end of life. In alignment with the direction established by the Group Product Manager and company objectives, this role translates direct customer and end-user insights, market opportunities, and competitive analysis into product priorities and requirements. The Product Manager leads product management and commercial activities within the company’s Stage-Gate process and works cross-functionally with engineering, sales, marketing, purchasing, operations, and finance to drive growth, profitability, competitiveness, and customer satisfaction.

**Essential Functions and Basic Duties**

* Manages the product line life cycle from opportunity identification and concept development through launch, sustainment, and end of life.
* Develops, maintains, and executes the strategy and prioritized roadmap for assigned product lines in alignment with the direction established by the Group Product Manager and company objectives. jobs.desc:
**JOB SUMMARY**

The Product Manager, TMS & Operational Communications owns the day-to-day product health, configuration, user experience, and continuous improvement of EASE’s core transportation management system and operational communications platforms. The lasting problem this role exists to solve: the systems EASE operators depend on every day are healthy, current, well configured, easy to use, and support freight moving without unnecessary friction.

Reporting to the VP / Head of Product Foundations, this role serves as the accountable product owner for McLeod and sits within the Operate function of EASE’s brokerage model (Sell, Buy, and Operate). The role owns TMS workflows, configuration, product experience, adoption, and the business-facing roadmap. Platform & Analytics owns the underlying McLeod database, infrastructure, performance, backup, recovery, and backend reliability.

Success is measured by TMS health, process compliance and business outcomes, not by the number of tickets closed or changes completed. McLeod and operational communications should enable employees to execute consistently, reduce manual workarounds, recover quickly from user-impacting issues, and contribute to SPEED (Shipments Per Ease Employee Daily), EASE’s north star operational metric.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES**

**TMS Product Strategy & Roadmap**

* Own the product roadmap for McLeod TMS, translating operational needs, recurring friction, vendor capabilities, and business priorities into a clear sequence of improvements.
* Maintain a living view of TMS capabilities, configuration, open issues, enhancement requests, and roadmap decisions so the organization has one source of truth for the health and direction of McLeod.
* Partner with the VP / Head of Product Foundations to determine when a need should be solved through McLeod configuration or capability versus another EASE product or platform.

**Outcome Ownership & Measurement**

* Own the outcome metrics for this role, such as user-impacting TMS issue volume and resolution time, workflow adoption, manual workarounds eliminated, release adoption, configuration quality, and operational communications service performance.
* Set each objective with a baseline, a target, a date, and a counter-metric, working with Platform & Analytics on metric definitions and instrumentation where needed.
* Report progress in terms of TMS health, user impact, and business outcomes. Ticket counts, configuration changes, and releases completed are not measures of success on their own.

**TMS Health & Lifecycle Management**

* Maintain a current health view of McLeod, including open defects, recurring user issues, support cases, version currency, configuration risks, license utilization, and vendor commitments.
* Own business-side triage and escalation for TMS issues, ensuring every material problem has a clear owner, priority, communication path, and path to resolution.
* Keep McLeod in good standing by proactively managing lifecycle needs, support status, release readiness, documentation, and known product risks before they become operational disruptions.

**Workflow, Configuration & User Experience**

* Own McLeod workflow and configuration decisions for EASE operations, working directly with users to understand how orders, dispatch, carrier assignment, status management, billing handoffs, and other core workflows are performed.
* Identify and resolve recurring friction, duplicate entry, unnecessary steps, and manual workarounds, and determine whether the right response is configuration, process change, training, vendor capability, or a separate EASE product.
* Maintain clear and consistent standards for TMS configuration and functional ownership so changes are intentional, documented, tested, and aligned with how EASE operates.
* Partner with Product Foundations, Operations, and affected product pillars when TMS workflow changes have downstream impact on AMMI, Forge, integrations, reporting, or other internal produ

jobs.desc:
**Position Overview:**

The Product Owner for Sierra Customer Charlie leads the development and continuous enhancement of HomeServe’s AI-powered virtual assistant (“Charlie”), built on the Sierra AI platform, which automates high-volume contact-center workflows across voice and chat. This role advances HomeServe’s automation and digital-transformation agenda—enabling customer self-service to reduce live-agent call volume, lower cost-to-serve, and improve the customer experience—and owns the full lifecycle for Charlie capabilities, from opportunity identification and High-Level Design (HLD) through integration, go-live, and operations.

The role requires close collaboration with business stakeholders (Automation, Contact Center, Marketing/Compliance) and technical partners (Solution Architecture, Mulesoft ESB, Sierra AI, IT Security). The Product Owner balances conversational-AI design with business strategy to deliver measurable value—e.g., automating payment updates, job triage and creation, and marketing-preference handling—defines the Charlie product vision, champions the customer conversational experience, and drives continuous improvement using containment, deflection, and satisfaction insights, aligned to HomeServe Enterprise Solution Architecture standards.

  

**Responsibilities:**

**Product Strategy**

* Define and drive product vision and strategy, from identification and planning, through to prioritization, solution design, development, and maintenance, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and user needs
* Analyze contact-center call drivers and automation opportunities to inform the Charlie product roadmap and prioritize high-volume, high-value use cases
* Engage with business stakeholders (Automation, Contact Center, Compliance) to gather insights, identify pain points, and ensure Charlie capabilities meet stakeholder and customer needs
* Lead review of conversation transcripts, containment/deflection data, and customer feedback, incorporating findings into the Charlie backlog

jobs.desc:
**About the Role**
==================

We are looking for a Product Manager who can turn a complicated, regulated domain into software that feels obvious to use. You will own a meaningful slice of the Scriptly platform end to end, from understanding what pharmacies and partners actually need through to what ships and how it performs once it is live.

This is a hands-on role on a small team, and you will not be handed a fully formed backlog. Expect to spend real time with pharmacists, technicians, our Support and Success teams, and enterprise partners, then decide what matters most and make the case for it. You will work with Engineering daily and have the latitude to shape your area rather than administer it.

Our current roadmap spans clinical and dispensing workflow improvements, pharmacy automation and robotics integration, interoperability work including Surescripts and TEFCA participation, and expansion of our hub pharmacy capabilities. There is more opportunity in front of us than any one quarter can absorb, so prioritization is a core part of the job.

**What You'll Do**
==================

**Own the Problem, Not Just the Backlog**
-----------------------------------------

* Develop deep knowledge of pharmacy operations and hub services, to the point where you can anticipate what customers need before they ask.
* Talk regularly with pharmacists, technicians, and pharmacy owners, and sit with our Support and Success teams to learn what actually generates friction.
* Translate customer needs, partner commitments, and regulatory requirements into clear problem statements and prioritized outcomes.
* Maintain and communicate a roadmap that leadership, Engineering, and customer-facing teams can all plan against.

**Define and Ship**
-------------------

* Write clear, complete requirements: user stories, acceptance criteria, workflows, edge cases, and the reasoning behind the decision.
* Partner closely with Engineering through refinement, sprint planning, and delivery, staying available to answer questions and make tradeoff calls quickly.
* Work with design and engineering on interfaces that respect how busy a pharmacy actually is.
* Own release readiness, including documentation, internal enablement, and coordination with Support and Success before anything reaches customers.

**Measure and Iterate**
-----------------------

* Define what success looks like before you build, then track it after launch.
* Use product analytics, ticket trends, and direct customer feedback to decide what to improve, what to leave alone, and what to retire.
* Bring evidence to prioritization conversations so decisions are based on impact rather than volume of requests.

**Partner Across the Company**
------------------------------

* Support enterprise and manufacturer partner engagements by translating contractual and operational commitments into deliverable product work.
* Keep Sales, Support, Success, and Operations informed on what is coming, what changed, and what it means for customers.
* Contribute to integration and interoperability initiatives with vendors, robotics manufacturers, and industry networks.

**Other Duties Assigned**
-------------------------

* Performs related duties in support of department goals
* Assists with special projects and initiatives as needed
* Supports team members and cross-functional tasks during peak periods
* Other related duties as required to meet operational objectives

=================================

* 3+ years of product management experience.
* Demonstrated ability to work through a complex domain and become the person others come to for answers.
* Strong written communication, especially the ability to write requirements engineers can build from without guessing.
* Comfort working directly with engineers day to day in an agile process, including backlog grooming in Jira or a similar tool.

**Position Overview**
=====================

Join our team as a Product Manager, Enrollment and own the technology that enables family caregivers to discover, enroll in, and onboard into Ceresti's dementia care program. This role develops and leads cross-functional initiatives to drive caregiver enrollment at scale, owning a roadmap that spans marketing and referral channel development, outbound call operations, CRM strategy, web and form experiences, and the onboarding journey onto our platform.

You will be the connective tissue between enrollment operations, marketing, clinical, and engineering where you will lead and influence without direct reporting lines. You will partner with operations to define and accelerate the end-to-end enrollment funnel: defining the metrics, instrumenting the analytics, running a continuous cadence of experiments, and shipping the products and automations that move conversion. You will own a roadmap of improvements to existing systems (e.g. AI-powered enrollment intelligence engine) as well as high-leverage, zero-to-one bets such as referral programs and self-serve onboarding. This is a role suited for a product manager who is growth-oriented, experiment-driven, scrappy, and energized by ambiguous, high-impact problem spaces with a direct line to business growth.

About Us & What We Do

Ceresti is on a mission to reduce avoidable hospitalizations and improve care for people living with dementia while improving the lives of their families and caregivers. We envision a world in which family caregivers of people living with dementia are supported and have the knowledge, skills, and confidence to provide the best possible care for their loved ones.

Ceresti is a tech-enabled dementia care provider with a differentiated model of care that improves outcomes and delivers guaranteed cost savings by including family caregivers in the care team. We offer health plans and accountable care organizations a turnkey solution for impacting a population that has limited engagement in traditional clinical programs.

Our culture is rooted in agility, innovation, and collaboration. We believe that every idea—no matter how small—can spark a meaningful improvement. Together, we create solutions that make a lasting impact on the healthcare ecosystem, enabling more compassionate and cost-effective care for those who need it most.

* Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the technology that drives caregiver enrollment, from first touch through activation on the Ceresti platform.
* Translate company growth targets into a prioritized, sequenced roadmap of enrollment initiatives.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is dedicated to developing AI assistants that are helpful, harmless, and honest. As usage of our AI services grows, we need to ensure they are not misused. The Safeguards team is at the forefront of protecting our users from the risks of powerful AIs as well as ethical, technical, and social risks from the use of generative AI. The Safeguards team at Anthropic builds protections for new AI features enabled by the research teams and protects new products and surfaces developed by our product teams. As a Product Manager for the Safeguards team at Anthropic, you will own the ideation, design, development and deployment of Safeguards systems and relevant product UX to ensure we are advancing frontier models safely to users across various cloud platforms. You will work closely with our research and product teams to develop detections, evals, interventions, and tools to measure and mitigate deployment and user risks. 

We are looking for a product manager who is deeply committed to making AI safe and beneficial for humanity.  You are aware of the risks and are committed to working with experts and coming up with ideas for Anthropic to implement. You have deep technical expertise in development, deployment and measurement of Safeguards systems. You thrive in rapidly moving and ambiguous environments.

  • Drive impact via ruthless prioritization by clearly defining problems, solution options forward, clarity on both business & technical tradeoffs and accordingly clear requirements toward MVP vs. ideal state.

jobs.title: Technical Product Marketing Manager

PhoenixAI is the Agentic AI Database, purpose-built to give autonomous AI agents sub-second access to live enterprise data at massive scale. The platform unifies real-time and at-rest data in a single AI-native engine, combining the speed and concurrency that agentic workloads demand with the governance and deployment flexibility enterprises require to put AI into production. Formerly known as CelerData, PhoenixAI is headquartered in Menlo Park, California. Learn more at phoenixdata.ai

About the role

We are seeking a Technical Product Marketing Manager to drive the technical content, developer evangelism, and sales enablement that bring PhoenixAI's Agentic Database to market. This is a hands-on, hybrid role at the intersection of product marketing and developer relations: you'll write about the product, speak about it to engineers and technical buyers, demo it live, and arm our sales team to sell it. The ideal candidate is an engineer at heart who can also write and speak — someone who has built with data systems and can translate that depth into content, talks, and enablement that resonate with technical audiences.

What you'll do

As our Technical Product Marketing Manager, you'll be a key contributor to PhoenixAI's go-to-market, working across four connected areas: content, evangelism, enablement, and launches. Your responsibilities include:

• Technical Content Creation: Research, write, and publish technical content — blog posts, tutorials, benchmarks, competitive comparisons, and solution briefs — that demonstrates product depth and drives awareness and adoption among engineers and technical buyers.

• Developer Evangelism & Speaking: Represent PhoenixAI and StarRocks to technical audiences — deliver webinars, speak at meetups and industry conferences, and present live product demos to prospects and at events.

• Sales Enablement: Build and deliver technical enablement for Sales and Solutions — pitch decks, battlecards, demo scripts, and FAQs — plus regular training sessions, new-hire onboarding, and competitive briefings that keep the field sharp on product and market.

• Messaging & Feedback Loop: Contribute to PhoenixAI's positioning and messaging across the open-source (StarRocks) and commercial offerings, and bring signals from the community, customers, and sales back to product and marketing to sharpen the narrative.

• Cross-Functional Partnership: Work closely with product management, engineering, sales, and marketing to keep content, demos, and enablement accurate, current, and grounded in real product capabilities.

• Hands-on software development experience; proficient in SQL and comfortable building and presenting live product demos.

• Strong technical foundation in databases, distributed systems, or lakehouse architectures; able to hold your own in technical conversations with engineers and technical buyers.
