About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We believe powerful AI can compress a century of scientific progress into a decade. Claude Science is a big part of building toward that future.

Claude Science is an AI workbench that gives researchers a single environment for work that today spans dozens of disconnected tools — literature, specialized databases, scientific computing, analysis, and publication-ready outputs. Claude Science already renders protein structures, genome tracks, and chemical structures natively, and coordinates multi-agent workflows with built-in review for citation and calculation errors — and we're just getting started. Much of this is being built 0→1 right now, in a category no one has defined yet.

We're growing the Claude Science product team. As a Product Manager on Claude Science, you will own a major area of the roadmap end to end — think expanding into new scientific fields, landing new model capabilities with researchers, or making the workbench ready for enterprise R&D teams — and help shape the overall product direction alongside the rest of the team. You'll spend real time with researchers in academic labs, biotech and pharma R&D, and research institutes to understand how science actually gets done — from hypothesis to analysis to publication and beyond— and turn what you learn into shipped product. You'll partner directly with our research teams to make the models better at science, help decide which fields and workflows we go after next, and shape what it takes for Claude Science to be trusted in enterprise and regulated research environments.

We're looking for experienced product managers and founders with real scientific or technical depth: people who can hold their own in a conversation with a structural biologist or a computational chemist, get in the weeds of model transcripts and evals, and still zoom out to help define a product category. You thrive in ambiguity, uncover non-obvious use cases for nascent capabilities, and bring those insights back to research.

Our north star is for Claude Science to accelerate scientific progress — across biology, chemistry, physics, and beyond — from early discovery through real-world application, by an order of magnitude.

Key responsibilities

  • Own vision, strategy, roadmap, and execution for a major area of Claude Science, and contribute to overall product direction in a category that is still being defined
  • Spend meaningful time with working scientists — in interviews, working sessions, and key customer conversations — and synthesize what you learn into clear priorities, requirements, and success metrics
  • Partner with research to make Claude better at science: define target behaviors, build and shape evals grounded in real scientific workflows, surface failure modes from real usage, and feed them back into model development
  • Drive model and feature launches in your area end to end: define readiness criteria, coordinate across research, engineering, design, and go-to-market, run early access programs, and make sure launches land well with researchers
  • Identify which scientific domains, data sources, tools, and integrations Claude Science should support next, and build the case with evidence from users, usage data, and the broader landscape
  • Prototype ideas yourself with Claude to validate them before committing engineering time
  • Work with safeguards, policy, security, and go-to-market partners

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Governments do some of the most consequential work there is: deciding benefits claims, getting veterans to care, investigating financial misconduct, running unemployment insurance, and producing the analysis that world leaders act on. Anthropic's public sector team exists to put Claude in the production path of that work. In the US and some allied governments, Claude is already in daily use across major agencies and US states.

The next steps need a particular kind of product manager: someone who can walk into an institution they have never worked with, sit with the people doing the work and find, alongside them, the workflow that matters. The best government products we know of started as an idea that came out of the room rather than a requirements document. 

The scope is large: a product portfolio here is a set of governments rather than a feature area. A year in, success looks like agencies delivering services more effectively because public servants are doing core parts of their job with Claude in the loop, and at least one thing that you learn from them shipping to every Anthropic enterprise. That is a lot of surface; you will have to choose where to go deep, and we will back the choice.

We are hiring across civilian, state and local, govtech, and national security portfolios and will match you to one on background and interest. Some portfolios require eligibility for a US security clearance, though most do not. You would be among the first product managers on the team, working with a dedicated engineering and research team and with the policy, go-to-market, customer success, and applied AI leads who already spend their days inside these agencies.

In this role, you will:

  • Alongside GTM, run discovery inside government institutions to find where Claude belongs in the production path of their work, then shape the product around what you find
  • Own product decisions for our government models and product offerings and the agency workflows built on top of them
  • Spot the government needs worth generalizing and carry them into Anthropic's broader roadmap. Many of Anthropic’s commercial features started as public-sector customer problems
  • Help Anthropic navigate government compliance regimes 
  • Partner with our cloud and integration partners 

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Have shipped successful products end-to-end. We weigh product judgment above any domain credential
  • Can point to something you built that was your idea: it came from watching people work rather than from a requirements document
  • Get things done through teams that don't report to you. In addition to the dedicated team, this role runs through a variety of partner teams inside Anthropic and many offices inside each agency.
  • Move on your own clock. You have shipped in an organization with a fast cadence, or you set the pace in an environment that didn't
  • Have built domain intuition fast in large enterprises that do not resemble each other
  • Are a US person. We have agreements with the US Government that mandate this for these roles.

Strong candidates may also have:

  • Roughly 7+ years building and shipping products, or equivalent scope
  • Real intuition for how government operates, earned either from the inside or at a digital services organization or by building products public servants actually use
  • Taken a public-sector or field requirement into a commercial product

This is a role for a strong executor with the ability to be agile in shipping in a 0-1 product space. Safe access is a new product that sits on the critical path of every model launch and every access program. Requirements arrive from many organizations at once, and most weeks you will be the person defining the problem rather than receiving it. 

Key responsibilities

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for the account and access primitives, with the goal that any team at Anthropic can provision access or run an access program with minimal support.   • Own the end-to-end experience of getting and managing access for internal stakeholders (research, model launches, safeguards, go-to-market) and for external customers and partners, and keep it consistent across every surface. jobs.title: Associate Product Manager
jobs.desc:
**About the role:**

We're looking for an Associate Product Manager to be Rezdy's dependable NA presence — covering the hours our Sydney/Melbourne-based PM and dev team aren't online. This is a strong fit for someone energized by operational rigor and real-time problem-solving: comfortable triaging under pressure, translating between technical and commercial audiences, and building product judgment by working closely alongside a senior PM rather than owning a roadmap from day one. Pacific timezone

**What you'll do:**

* Connect the time zones. Be the dependable daily link between North America stakeholders — support and account management teams — and the Sydney/Melbourne-based PM and dev team, flagging decisions and blockers in real time rather than letting them wait for the next overlap window.
* Be the NA distribution conduit for Commercial leads and distribution partners (Viator, GYG, etc) and Distribution Resellers
* Keep incidents moving and visible during NA hours. Triage escalations that occur in NA working hours against a defined severity framework, looping in the senior PM and dev lead when judgment calls exceed current scope, and making sure NA support and AM teams get clear, live updates rather than waiting for the next AU working day.
* Surface and track AM churn risk. Own intake of NA account-manager-flagged churn risk — capturing impact and urgency the moment it's raised — so it's framed and ready to compete fairly when the senior PM and dev lead plan the sprint.
* Answer for what's in flight. Be NA's go-to for "is this expected / is this known / what's the status" questions on Booking Manager and Distribution, working from close sync with the senior PM's roadmap and known-issues context rather than independent authority over it.
* Share release communication in NA hours. Help execute the existing release process — communication and post-release follow-up specifically during NA hours — rather than owning release planning or prioritization.
* Partner with Engineering at a working level. Build enough fluency in our data architecture to relay NA-side context accurately to engineering, without owning technical trade-off decisions.
* Put AI tools to work. Use AI tools to speed up research, troubleshooting, and day-to-day tasks — a lever for moving faster, not a replacement for judgment.

**What you'll bring:**

* 2+ years of experience in product management, product operations, or a closely related operational/customer-facing role, ideally in B2B SaaS.
* Comfort working within another PM's priorities and roadmap — bringing your own judgment and context to how that work gets executed
* Experience with incident or issue management processes, and communicating through them clearly under time pressure.
* Comfort working with legacy technology systems and the teams that maintain them — able to translate between legacy constraints and current product priorities for both engineering and commercial audiences.
* Strong written communication skills — able to adjust tone and depth for audiences ranging from support and account management teams to engineering.
* Ease operating in process-driven environments (Jira, Slack, or equivalent).
* Comfort picking up domain concepts across different product types — e.g., transactional booking flows versus distribution/channel connectivity — without needing deep expertise in both on day one.

**Nice to have:**

* Experience in the travel, tours, or activities booking software space.
* Familiarity with multi-brand or multi-product portfolios (Expedition Software operates Checkfront, Rezdy, and Regiondo).
* Prior experience in a support, account management, or customer-facing product role.

The salary range for this position is $80,000-$95,000, commensurate with years of experience, skillset, and qualifications.

**Role Summary:**
=================

The Product Owner I is responsible for the technical life cycle of the products they have been assigned, including coordinating development efforts, configuration changes, and support. The Product Owner I is responsible for documenting technical requirements, building product roadmaps, and budgeting associated with the products they oversee. The Product Owner I will collaborate with internal stakeholders, developers, and vendors regularly to deliver new products and enhance existing products that meet the documented business objectives of the products they support. Operate with oversight, ensuring a steady flow of user stories ready for development one (1) to two (2) weeks in advance

Define features and epics to communicate alignment with business objectives and to establish the scope of development that supports strategic goals
* Collect and understand technical requirements for new implementations and enhancements to ensure sufficient technical runway, minimize technical debt, and maintain the product

As Associate Product Manager of Data & Internal Systems, you will partner with Accounting, Operations, and IT to map, challenge, and continuously improve how our internal platforms work—from the moment data enters a system to how it’s stored, categorized, and consumed by downstream applications and teams. You deploy problem-first product thinking. This is not a role that rebuilds systems for the sake of modernization. You will understand root problems to solve and diagnose whether a new purpose-built application is needed or if an entire process needs to be reimagined. You will report directly to the Senior Product Manager of Technology and Platforms. What You’ll Own Investigate process and application pain points with Accounting, Finance, Operations, and IT before proposing any solution; solutions should solve problems, not replace systems Understand end-to-end process and data lifecycles, from input sources through storage, transformation, categorization, and application output to identify inefficiencies and where ambiguity occur Serve as a consistent, trusted point of contact for Accounting, Operations, Data Analytics and IT on internal system needs, including the ERP and roadmap priorities Work cross-departmentally to understand data flow gaps, identify repetitive or judgment-light internal workflows that are candidates for AI-assisted automation, light-weight applications or intelligent routing Understand InterPark’s data framework, any dependencies and their downstream impact and be part of InterPark’s AI-integration Facilitate cross-functional working sessions to align on process design and build consensus on change initiatives Be able to write product requirements and work with IT on building internal software applications Define success metrics for initiatives including time saved, improved business analysis, and productivity Ways of Working You ask “why does this process exist” before asking “how do we automate it” You communicate clearly in writing; requirements, status updates, and decision rationale are crisp and unambiguous You can write a good AI prompt and critically evaluate its output. **About CodeHS**
----------------

CodeHS is a comprehensive platform helping K-12 schools teach computer science. We provide curriculum, professional development, and a full software platform. CodeHS is used by millions of students and thousands of schools and districts around the US and the world.

**Mission**
-----------

**The mission of CodeHS is to empower all students to meaningfully impact the future.** We believe that in the 21st century, coding is a foundational skill, just like reading and writing. That’s why we say: **Read, Write, Code.** Coding and computer science are essential skills for students to learn and schools to teach.

### **Location**

**Chicago — our River North office, five days a week.** Reports to Zach Galant, CTO & co-founder.

CodeHS is hybrid overall. We have people in other offices and people who work remotely, and you’ll work with them regularly. This role is in person because it depends on coming up to speed quickly — on the product, on our customers, and on how the engineering team works — and that happens faster sitting next to people. So does mentorship. We want someone who wants to work that way and is excited about getting to work in person in the office.

We are growing our product team within engineering

We have about fifteen engineers in small project teams that re-form each cycle, and we ship constantly. What limits our impact usually isn’t engineering capacity — it’s conviction about what to build, why, and how to communicate it to the rest of the team and our customers. We want someone who can get that conviction from teachers, districts, the market, our data, and our own team, and turn it into something engineering can act on.

### **The role**

This role is for someone earlier in their career who wants to learn product management by doing it.

You’ll own projects within a product area, from understanding the problem through launch and adoption. You’ll make the calls on scope, specs, and tradeoffs for your projects and work closely with the engineers building them. The bigger calls — which problems to take on, and what not to build — we’ll make together at first, and more of them become yours as you show judgment.

You’ll sit in on the conversations where we set priorities across teams, so you can see how those decisions get made.

### **How you work**

**You build.** When you have an idea, go make a version of it. Not production code — a working prototype you drove an AI coding agent to build. Engineers review and take it to completion.

**You write things down.** Specs, product briefs, the reasoning behind a decision. If it isn’t written down here, it doesn’t count.

**You talk to the people who use this.** Much of the work is strategy and synthesis. But when the answer is in a classroom or on a call with a district, you go. It isn’t a heavy travel role, but you will need to join calls, talk to people on the team and customers, and build an understanding beyond just reasoning through things on your own.

**You connect engineering to everyone else.** Sales, customer success, support, and curriculum all have product or tooling needs. Your job is to gather the information, synthesize it, and use that to inform what the right things are to build.

### **You should be**

**Early in your career, with real work behind you.** At least a year of full-time work experience, in any role. A product management internship counts too. You don’t need to have been a PM.

**Comfortable around code,** without necessarily having been an engineer. You can read a pull request and ask an engineer good questions about how something works and what it would take to change.

**Fluent with AI, and adaptive to how things are changing.** You use AI to guide your thinking and move quickly, but you don’t hide behind it for judgment. What the Role Entails
About The Company
Tencent is a leading global technology company focused on connecting people and developing innovative products and services that improve the quality of life of people around the world. Founded in 1998 and publicly traded on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange since 2004, Tencent offers a variety of products and services, including leading communication and social platforms (Weixin/WeChat), high-quality entertainment (from video games, music, TV and film, sport and literature), FinTech (WeChat Pay and QQ Wallet) and industry-leading cloud products and services.
Cloud & Smart Industries Group (CSIG) is responsible for promoting the company's cloud and industry Internet strategy. CSIG explores the interactions between users and industries to create innovative solutions for smart industries via technological advancements such as cloud, AI, and network security. While driving the digitalization of retail, medical, education, transportation and other industries, CSIG helps companies serve users in smarter ways, building a new ecosystem of intelligent industries that connect users and businesses.
Position Overview
With our strong international growth, Tencent Cloud International is thrilled to offer an exciting opportunity for passionate undergraduates / graduate students to join our CPaaS Product Management Internship. As part of the team, you'll have the chance to collaborate with industry experts, contribute to product design and operations, and gain invaluable experience in shaping the future of communication platforms. This internship provides hands-on learning, mentorship, and the opportunity to make a real impact in a global market.

• Participate in the design of CPaaS products, contributing to framework, function, and interaction design under the guidance of experienced product managers.

• Conduct research on market trends, industry developments, and competitor analysis to provide valuable insights for product decision-making.

• Assist in drafting product requirement documents and related documentation to communicate product vision and features effectively.

• Engage in product operations and promotional activities, supporting the team in driving product awareness and adoption.

Who We Look For

• Final-year undergraduates / graduate students majoring in technology, management, economics, computer science, or its equivalents with a vision to pursue his/her product management career path in public cloud industry. Relevant product management certifications would be advantageous.

• Able to commit at least 6-month full-time

• Demonstrate creativity, strong logical thinking, and exceptional problem-solving abilities, coupled with excellent communication skills.

• Passionate about product management, with a keen interest in researching various products and a focus on enhancing user experience.

• Proficiency in common product tools such as Microsoft Office, prototyping, and flowchart design software.

• Strong command in both English and Chinese Mandarin in order to communicate with China-headquarters based stakeholders and perform translation on product materials.

• Previous experience in B2B product internships, particularly in PaaS or SaaS, is preferred but not mandatory.
